301.s:
agnir uvāca
vākkarmapārśvayukśukratokakṛte mato plavaḥ /
hutāntā deśavarṇeyaṃ vidyā mukhyā sarasvatī //
:n
1 dhārya ceti kha..
2 vidyutpātavidhāviti gha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 114
301.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वाक्कर्मपार्श्वयुक्शुक्रतोककृते मतो प्लवः /
हुतान्ता देशवर्णेयं विद्या मुख्या सरस्वती //
:न्
1 धार्य चेति ख..
2 विद्युत्पातविधाविति घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 114
301.m:
Agni said:
Joined with speech and action on both sides, for the sake of the offspring of Śukra, a vessel is considered;
ending with fire, this is the prime vidyā Sarasvatī of the region's letters.
[Notes]
1. ‘dhārya ca’ in manuscript kha.
2. ‘vidyutpātavidhau’ in manuscripts gha, ja, ña, and ṭa.
p. 114

301.s:
akṣārāśī varṇalakṣaṃ japet samatimān bhavet /
atriḥ savahnirvāmākṣivindurindrāya hṛtparaḥ //
301.d:
अक्षाराशी वर्णलक्षं जपेत् समतिमान् भवेत् /
अत्रिः सवह्निर्वामाक्षिविन्दुरिन्द्राय हृत्परः //
301.m:
One should recite one hundred thousand letters continuously; one becomes endowed with good intellect.
Atri with Agni, the left eye, and the bindu; followed by the heart for Indra.

301.s:
vajrapadmadharaṃ śakraṃ pītamāvāhya pūjayet /
niyutaṃ homayedājyatilāṃstenābhiṣecayet //
301.d:
वज्रपद्मधरं शक्रं पीतमावाह्य पूजयेत् /
नियुतं होमयेदाज्यतिलांस्तेनाभिषेचयेत् //
301.m:
Having invoked yellow Indra bearing the thunderbolt and the lotus, one should worship him.
One should offer a million clarified butter and sesamum oblations, and consecrate him with that.

301.s:
nṛpādirbhraṣṭarajyādīnrājyaputrādimāpnuyāt /
hṛllekhā śaktidevākhyā doṣāgnirdaṇḍidaṇḍavān //
301.d:
नृपादिर्भ्रष्टरज्यादीन्राज्यपुत्रादिमाप्नुयात् /
हृल्लेखा शक्तिदेवाख्या दोषाग्निर्दण्डिदण्डवान् //
301.m:
A king or similar person fallen from his kingdom obtains his kingdom, sons, and the like.
The Hṛllekhā is named the Śakti deity; the fire of fault, having a staff and a punisher.

301.s:
śivamiṣṭvā japecchaktimaṣṭamyādicaturdaśīṃ /
cakrapāśāṅkuśadharāṃ sābhayāṃ varadāyikāṃ //
301.d:
शिवमिष्ट्वा जपेच्छक्तिमष्टम्यादिचतुर्दशीं /
चक्रपाशाङ्कुशधरां साभयां वरदायिकां //
301.m:
Having worshipped Śiva, one should recite the Śakti [mantra] from the eighth to the fourteenth [lunar day]—
[meditating on her] bearing a discus, noose, and goad, accompanied by the gesture of fearlessness, and granting boons.

301.s:
homādinā ca saubhāgyaṃ kavitvaṃ puravān bhavet /
oṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ kāmāya sarvajanahitāya sarvajanamohanāya
prajvalitāya sarvajanahṛdayaṃ mamātmagataṃ kuru 2 oṃ
etajjapādinā mantrao vaśayet sakalaṃ jagat //
oṃ hrīṃ cāmuṇḍe amukandaha 2 paca 2 mama vaśamānaya 2 ṭha
2
301.d:
होमादिना च सौभाग्यं कवित्वं पुरवान् भवेत् /
ओं ह्रीं ओं नमः कामाय सर्वजनहिताय सर्वजनमोहनाय
प्रज्वलिताय सर्वजनहृदयं ममात्मगतं कुरु 2 ओं
एतज्जपादिना मन्त्रओ वशयेत् सकलं जगत् //
ओं ह्रीं चामुण्डे अमुकन्दह 2 पच 2 मम वशमानय 2 ठ
2
301.m:
By fire oblation and other rites, one attains good fortune, poetic skill, and becomes master of a city.
“Oṃ hrīṃ oṃ, obeisance to Kāma, who brings welfare to all beings, who enchants all beings, who is blazing forth; bring the heart of all beings into my power! Bring it! Oṃ.”
Through recitation and other practices with this mantra, one can subjugate the entire world.
“Oṃ hrīṃ Cāmuṇḍā, burn so-and-so! Burn! Cook! Cook! Bring [them] into my subjugation! Bring [them]! Ṭha ṭha!”

301.s:
vaśīkaraṇakṛnmantraścāmuṇḍāyāḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
phalatrayakaṣāyeṇa varāṅgaṃ kṣālayedvaśe //
301.d:
वशीकरणकृन्मन्त्रश्चामुण्डायाः प्रकीर्तितः /
फलत्रयकषायेण वराङ्गं क्षालयेद्वशे //
301.m:
This is proclaimed as the subjugation mantra of Cāmuṇḍā.
For subjugation, one should wash the pudendum with a decoction of the three fruits.

301.s:
aśvagandhāyavaiḥ strī tu niśākarpūrakādinā /
pippalītaṇḍulānyaṣṭau maricāni ca viṃśatiḥ //
301.d:
अश्वगन्धायवैः स्त्री तु निशाकर्पूरकादिना /
पिप्पलीतण्डुलान्यष्टौ मरिचानि च विंशतिः //
301.m:
A woman [is subjugated] by aśvagandhā and barley with turmeric, camphor, and other [ingredients],
eight grains of long pepper, and twenty black peppercorns.

301.s:
vṛhatīrasalepaś ca vaśe syānmaraṇāntikaṃ /
kaṭīramūlatrikaṭukṣaudralepas tathā bhavet //
301.d:
वृहतीरसलेपश् च वशे स्यान्मरणान्तिकं /
कटीरमूलत्रिकटुक्षौद्रलेपस् तथा भवेत् //
301.m:
Anointment with the juice of bṛhatī brings about subjugation until death;
likewise, an anointment of the root of kaṭīra, trikatu, and honey will do so.

301.s:
himaṃ kapitthakarabhaṃ māgadhī madhukaṃ madhu /
teṣāṃ lepaḥ prayuktastu dampatyoḥ svastimāvahet //
301.d:
हिमं कपित्थकरभं मागधी मधुकं मधु /
तेषां लेपः प्रयुक्तस्तु दम्पत्योः स्वस्तिमावहेत् //
301.m:
Camphor, wood-apple shoot, long pepper, madhuka, and honey—
anointment of these applied brings welfare to husband and wife.

301.s:
saśarkarayonilepāt kadambarasako madhu /
sahadevī mahālakṣmīḥ putrajīvī kṛtāñjaliḥ //
:p 115
301.d:
सशर्करयोनिलेपात् कदम्बरसको मधु /
सहदेवी महालक्ष्मीः पुत्रजीवी कृताञ्जलिः //
:प् 115
301.m:
By anointment of the vagina with sugar, juice of kadamba, and honey,
sahadevī, mahālakṣmī, putrajīvī, and kṛtāñjali—
p. 115

301.s:
etaccūrṇaṃ śiraḥkṣiptaṃ likasya vaśamuttamam /
triphalācandanakvāthaprasthā dvikuḍavam pṛthak //
301.d:
एतच्चूर्णं शिरःक्षिप्तं लिकस्य वशमुत्तमम् /
त्रिफलाचन्दनक्वाथप्रस्था द्विकुडवम् पृथक् //
301.m:
this powder thrown upon the head yields supreme subjugation of a person.
A prastha of the decoction of triphalā and sandalwood, and two kuḍavas each

301.s:
bhṛṅgahemarasandoṣātāvatī cuñcukaṃ madhu /
ghṛtaiḥ pakvā niśā chāyā śuṣkā lipyā tu rañjanī //
301.d:
भृङ्गहेमरसन्दोषातावती चुञ्चुकं मधु /
घृतैः पक्वा निशा छाया शुष्का लिप्या तु रञ्जनी //
301.m:
of juice of bhṛṅgarāja, gold, juice of nightshade, cuñcuka, and honey,
cooked with clarified butter, dried in the shade of night; this paste is delightful.

301.s:
vidārīṃ soccaṭāmāṣacūrṇībhhtāṃ saśarkarāṃ /
gathitāṃ yaḥ vipet kṣīrair nityaṃ strīśatakaṃ vrajet //
301.d:
विदारीं सोच्चटामाषचूर्णीभ्ह्तां सशर्करां /
गथितां यः विपेत् क्षीरैर् नित्यं स्त्रीशतकं व्रजेत् //
301.m:
One who drinks powder of vidārī, uccaṭā, and black gram, mixed with sugar
and cooked in milk, can continuously visit a hundred women.

301.s:
gulmamāṣatilavrīhicūrṇakṣīrasitānvitaṃ /
aśvatthavaṃśadarbhāṇāṃ mūlaṃ vai vaiṣṇavīśniyoḥ //
301.d:
गुल्ममाषतिलव्रीहिचूर्णक्षीरसितान्वितं /
अश्वत्थवंशदर्भाणां मूलं वै वैष्णवीश्नियोः //
301.m:
Mixed with milk and sugar, the powder of gulma, black gram, sesamum, and rice,
and the root of aśvattha, bamboo, and darbha grass, for Vaiṣṇavī and Śrī.

301.s:
mūlaṃ dūrvāśvagandhotthaṃ pivet kṣīraiḥ sutārthinī /
kauntīlakṣmyāḥ śiphā dhātrī vajraṃ loghnaṃ vaṭāṅkuram //
301.d:
मूलं दूर्वाश्वगन्धोत्थं पिवेत् क्षीरैः सुतार्थिनी /
कौन्तीलक्ष्म्याः शिफा धात्री वज्रं लोघ्नं वटाङ्कुरम् //
301.m:
A woman desiring a son should drink milk with the root derived from dūrvā and aśvagandhā;
the root of kauntī, lakṣmī, myrobalan, vajra, iron-destroyer, and a shoot of the banyan tree.

301.s:
ājyakṣīramṛtau peyaṃ putrārthaṃ tridivaṃ striyā /
putrārthinī pivet kṣīraṃ śrīmūlaṃ savaṭāṅkuram //
301.d:
आज्यक्षीरमृतौ पेयं पुत्रार्थं त्रिदिवं स्त्रिया /
पुत्रार्थिनी पिवेत् क्षीरं श्रीमूलं सवटाङ्कुरम् //
301.m:
It should be drunk by a woman for three days in clarified butter, milk, and nectar for the sake of a son.
A woman desiring a son should drink milk with bilva root and a banyan shoot.

301.s:
śrīvaḍāṅkuradevīnāṃ rasaṃ nasye vipecca sā /
śrīpadmamūlamutkṣīramaśvatthottaramūlayuk //
301.d:
श्रीवडाङ्कुरदेवीनां रसं नस्ये विपेच्च सा /
श्रीपद्ममूलमुत्क्षीरमश्वत्थोत्तरमूलयुक् //
301.m:
She should drink or use as nasal drops the juice of bilva, banyan shoot, and the goddess [plant];
the root of white lotus with milk, joined with the northern root of an aśvattha tree,

301.s:
taralaṃ payasā yuktaṃ kārpāsaphalapallvaṃ /
apāmārgasya puṣpāgraṃ navaṃ samahiṣīpayaḥ //
301.d:
तरलं पयसा युक्तं कार्पासफलपल्ल्वं /
अपामार्गस्य पुष्पाग्रं नवं समहिषीपयः //
301.m:
liquid mixed with milk, cotton fruit sprout,
and fresh tip of an apāmārga flower together with buffalo milk.

301.s:
putrārthañcārdhaṣaṭśākair yogāś catvāra īritāḥ /
śarkarotpalapuṣpākṣalodhracandanasārivāḥ //
301.d:
पुत्रार्थञ्चार्धषट्शाकैर् योगाश् चत्वार ईरिताः /
शर्करोत्पलपुष्पाक्षलोध्रचन्दनसारिवाः //
301.m: And four formulations are declared with three herbs for obtaining a son: / sugar, water-lily flower, bibhītaka, lodhra, sandalwood, and sārivā.

301.s:
sravamāṇe striyā garbhe dātavyāstaṇḍulāmbhasā /
lājā yaṣṭisitādrākṣākṣaudrasarpīṃṣi vā lihet //
301.d:
स्रवमाणे स्त्रिया गर्भे दातव्यास्तण्डुलाम्भसा /
लाजा यष्टिसिताद्राक्षाक्षौद्रसर्पींषि वा लिहेत् //
301.m: When a woman is having a miscarriage, they should be given with rice water. / Or she should lick puffed grain, liquorice, white sugar, grapes, honey, and ghee.

301.s:
aṭaruṣakalāṅgulyaḥ kākamācyāḥ śiphā pṛthak /
nābheradhaḥ samālipya prasūte pramadā sukham //
301.d:
अटरुषकलाङ्गुल्यः काकमाच्याः शिफा पृथक् /
नाभेरधः समालिप्य प्रसूते प्रमदा सुखम् //
301.m: Vāsā, kalāṅguli, and the root of kākamācī applied separately / below the navel, a woman gives birth with ease.

301.s:
raktaṃ śuklaṃ jāvāpuṣpaṃ raktaśuklastrutau pivet /
:p 116
keśaraṃ vṛhatīmūlaṃ gopīyaṣṭitṛṇotpalam //
301.d:
रक्तं शुक्लं जावापुष्पं रक्तशुक्लस्त्रुतौ पिवेत् /
:प् 116
केशरं वृहतीमूलं गोपीयष्टितृणोत्पलम् //
301.m:
One should drink red [and] white hibiscus flowers during red [or] white vaginal discharge.
[Page 116]
Saffron, bṛhatī root, anantamūla, liquorice, tṛṇotpala,

301.s:
sājakṣīraṃ satailaṃ tadbhakṣaṇaṃ romajanmakṛt /
śīryamāṇeṣu keśeṣu sthāpanañca bhavedidam //
301.d:
साजक्षीरं सतैलं तद्भक्षणं रोमजन्मकृत् /
शीर्यमाणेषु केशेषु स्थापनञ्च भवेदिदम् //
301.m: eaten with goat's milk and oil, causes the growth of hair. / And when the hair is falling out, this serves to stabilise it.

301.s:
dhātrībhṛṅgarasaprasthatailañca kṣiramāḍhakam /
oṃ namo bhagavate tryambakāya upaśamaya 2 culu 2 mili 2 bhida 2 gomānini
cakriṇi hrūṃ phaṭ ||
asmin grāme gokulasya rakṣāṃ kuru 2 śāntiṃ kuru 2 //
ghaṇḍākarṇo mahāseno vīraḥ prokto mahābalaḥ //
301.d:
धात्रीभृङ्गरसप्रस्थतैलञ्च क्षिरमाढकम् /
ओं नमो भगवते त्र्यम्बकाय उपशमय 2 चुलु 2 मिलि 2 भिद 2 गोमानिनि
चक्रिणि ह्रूं फट् ||
अस्मिन् ग्रामे गोकुलस्य रक्षां कुरु 2 शान्तिं कुरु 2 //
घण्डाकर्णो महासेनो वीरः प्रोक्तो महाबलः //
301.m:
A prastha of āmalakī and bhṛṅgarāja juice with oil, and an āḍhaka of milk.
Oṃ, obeisance to the blessed Tryambaka! Calm, calm! Culu, culu! Mili, mili! Bhida, bhida! O Gomāninī, / O bearer of the discus! Hrūṃ phaṭ!
In this village, protect, protect the herd of cows! Make peace, make peace!
Ghaṇṭākarṇa, Mahāsena, declared to be heroic and of great strength,

301.s:
mārīnirnāśanakaraḥ sa māṃ pātu jagatpatiḥ /
ślokau caiva nyasedetau mantrau gorakṣakau pṛthak //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānāmantrā nāmaikādhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha dvyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
aṅgākṣarārcanam
301.d:
मारीनिर्नाशनकरः स मां पातु जगत्पतिः /
श्लोकौ चैव न्यसेदेतौ मन्त्रौ गोरक्षकौ पृथक् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानामन्त्रा नामैकाधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ द्व्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
अङ्गाक्षरार्चनम्
301.m:
the destroyer of pestilence, may that lord of the world protect me! / One should deposit these two verses separately as mantras protecting cattle.
Thus ends the three hundred and first chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'Various Mantras'.
Now, the three hundred and second chapter.
Worship of the Syllables of the Body.

302.s:
agnir uvāca
yadā janmarkṣagaś candro bhānuḥ saptasarāśigaḥ /
pauṣṇaḥ kālaḥ sa vijñeyastadā grāsaṃ parīkṣayet //
302.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
यदा जन्मर्क्षगश् चन्द्रो भानुः सप्तसराशिगः /
पौष्णः कालः स विज्ञेयस्तदा ग्रासं परीक्षयेत् //
302.m: Agni said: / When the moon is in the natal asterism and the sun is in the seventh sign, / that is to be known as the time of death; then one should observe the seizure [of death].

302.s:
kaṇṭoṣṭhau calataḥsthānādyasya vakrā ca nāsikā /
kṛṣṇā ca jihvā saptāhaṃ jīvitaṃ tasya vai bhavet //
302.d:
कण्टोष्ठौ चलतःस्थानाद्यस्य वक्रा च नासिका /
कृष्णा च जिह्वा सप्ताहं जीवितं तस्य वै भवेत् //
302.m: He whose throat and lips move from their place, whose nose is twisted, / and whose tongue is black, his life indeed lasts seven days.

302.s:
tāro meṣo viṣaṃ dantī naro dīrgho vaṇā rasaḥ /
krūddholkāya maholkāya vīrolkāya śikhā bhavet //
:p 117
302.d:
तारो मेषो विषं दन्ती नरो दीर्घो वणा रसः /
क्रूद्धोल्काय महोल्काय वीरोल्काय शिखा भवेत् //
:प् 117
302.m:
[By combining the codes for] tāra, meṣa, viṣa, dantī, nara, the long [vowel], vaṇā, and rasa: / to Krūddholka, to Maholka, to Vīrolka, [there] should be the crest-mantra,
[Page 117]

302.s:
hyalkāya rāhasolkāya vaiṣṇavoṣṭākṣaro manuḥ /
kaniṣṭhāditadaṣṭānāmaṅgulīnāñca parvasu //
302.d:
ह्यल्काय राहसोल्काय वैष्णवोष्टाक्षरो मनुः /
कनिष्ठादितदष्टानामङ्गुलीनाञ्च पर्वसु //
302.m: to Dyulkā, to Rāhasolka—this is the eight-syllable mantra of Viṣṇu. / On the joints of the eight fingers starting from the little finger,

302.s:
jyeṣṭhāgreṇa kramāttāvan mūrdhanyaṣṭākṣaraṃ nyaset /
tarjanyāntāramaṅguṣṭhe lagne madhyamayā ca tat //
302.d:
ज्येष्ठाग्रेण क्रमात्तावन् मूर्धन्यष्टाक्षरं न्यसेत् /
तर्जन्यान्तारमङ्गुष्ठे लग्ने मध्यमया च तत् //
302.m: with the tip of the thumb in sequence, one should deposit the eight-syllable mantra on the head. / In the gap of the forefinger, joined to the thumb, and with the middle finger,

302.s:
taleṅguṣṭhe taduttāraṃ vījottāraṃ tato nyaset /
raktagauradhūmraharijjātarūpāḥ sitāstrayaḥ //
302.d:
तलेङ्गुष्ठे तदुत्तारं वीजोत्तारं ततो न्यसेत् /
रक्तगौरधूम्रहरिज्जातरूपाः सितास्त्रयः //
302.m: on the palm, on the thumb—having uttered it, one should then deposit the root-seed. / Red, white, smoke-coloured, yellow, golden, and three white:
one should sequentially deposit these letters having such forms, mentally conceived, / on the heart, face, eyes, head, feet, palate, genitals, hands, and other [limbs].

302.s:
aṅgāni ca nyasedvījānnyasyātha karadehayoḥ /
yathātmani tathā deve nyāsaḥ kāryaḥ karaṃ vinā //
302.d:
अङ्गानि च न्यसेद्वीजान्न्यस्याथ करदेहयोः /
यथात्मनि तथा देवे न्यासः कार्यः करं विना //
302.m: And one should deposit the limbs, having deposited the seed-syllables on the hands and body. / As in oneself, so too on the deity, the ritual deposition is to be done, except for the hands.

302.s:
hṛdādisthānagān varṇān gandhapuṣpai samarcayet /
dharmādyagnyādyadharmādi gātre pīṭhe 'mbuje nyaset //
302.d:
हृदादिस्थानगान् वर्णान् गन्धपुष्पै समर्चयेत् /
धर्माद्यग्न्याद्यधर्मादि गात्रे पीठे ऽम्बुजे न्यसेत् //
302.m: One should worship the letters located in the places such as the heart with perfumes and flowers. / One should deposit dharma and so forth in the south-east and other [directions], and adharma and so forth on the body, on the pedestal, and on the lotus.

302.s:
yatra keśarakiñjalkavyāpisūryendudāhināṃ /
maṇḍalantritayantāvad bhedaistatra nyaset kramāt //
302.d:
यत्र केशरकिञ्जल्कव्यापिसूर्येन्दुदाहिनां /
मण्डलन्त्रितयन्तावद् भेदैस्तत्र न्यसेत् क्रमात् //
302.m: Where the three maṇḍalas of the sun, moon, and fire pervade the filaments and anthers, / one should deposit them in sequence according to the divisions.

302.s:
guṇāś ca tantrasatvādyāḥ keśarasthāś ca śaktayaḥ /
vimalotkarṣaṇījñānakriyāyogāś ca vai kramāt //
302.d:
गुणाश् च तन्त्रसत्वाद्याः केशरस्थाश् च शक्तयः /
विमलोत्कर्षणीज्ञानक्रियायोगाश् च वै क्रमात् //
302.m: And the qualities sattva and so forth according to the Tantra, and the powers situated on the filaments: / Vimalā, Utkarṣiṇī, Jñānā, Kriyā, and Yogā in sequence,

302.s:
prahvī satyā tatheśānānugrahā madhyatastataḥ /
yogapīṭhaṃ samabhyarcya samāvahya hariṃ yajet //
302.d:
प्रह्वी सत्या तथेशानानुग्रहा मध्यतस्ततः /
योगपीठं समभ्यर्च्य समावह्य हरिं यजेत् //
302.m: Prahvī, Satyā, likewise Īśānā, Anugrahā, and then in the centre. / Having worshipped the yogic seat and invoked Hari, one should sacrifice.

302.s:
pādyārghyācamanīyañca pītavastravibhūṣaṇaṃ /
etat pañcopacārañca sarvaṃ mūlena dīyate //
302.d:
पाद्यार्घ्याचमनीयञ्च पीतवस्त्रविभूषणं /
एतत् पञ्चोपचारञ्च सर्वं मूलेन दीयते //
302.m: Foot-water, water offering, water for sipping, yellow garment, and ornament— / this fivefold offering, everything is presented with the root mantra.

302.s:
vāsudevādayaḥ pūjyāś catvāro dikṣu mūrtayaḥ /
vidikṣu śrīsarasvatyai ratiśāntyai ca pūjayet //
:n
1 hṛdāsyanetramūrdhāṅghrijānuguhyakarādiṣviti kha..
:p 118
302.d:
वासुदेवादयः पूज्याश् चत्वारो दिक्षु मूर्तयः /
विदिक्षु श्रीसरस्वत्यै रतिशान्त्यै च पूजयेत् //
:न्
1 हृदास्यनेत्रमूर्धाङ्घ्रिजानुगुह्यकरादिष्विति ख..
:प् 118
302.m:
The four forms, Vāsudeva and the others, are to be worshipped in the cardinal directions. / In the intermediate directions, one should worship Śrī, Sarasvatī, Rati, and Śānti.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: hṛdāsyanetramūrdhāṅghrijānuguhyakarādiṣviti kha..] [Page 118]

302.s:
śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ muṣalaṃ khaḍgaśārṅgike /
vanamālānvitaṃ dikṣu vidikṣu ca yajet kramāt //
302.d:
शङ्खं चक्रं गदां पद्मं मुषलं खड्गशार्ङ्गिके /
वनमालान्वितं दिक्षु विदिक्षु च यजेत् क्रमात् //
302.m: Conch, discus, mace, lotus, pestle, sword, bow, / together with the garland of wild flowers, one should worship in the cardinal and intermediate directions in order.

302.s:
abhyarcya ca vahistārkṣyaṃ devasya purato 'rcayet /
viśvaksenañca someśaṃ madhye āvaraṇādvahiḥ(1) /
indrādiparicāreṇa pūjya sarvamavāpnuyāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe aṅgākṣarārcanaṃ nāma
dvyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha tryadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
pañcākṣarādipūjāmantrāḥ
302.d:
अभ्यर्च्य च वहिस्तार्क्ष्यं देवस्य पुरतो ऽर्चयेत् /
विश्वक्सेनञ्च सोमेशं मध्ये आवरणाद्वहिः(1) /
इन्द्रादिपरिचारेण पूज्य सर्वमवाप्नुयात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अङ्गाक्षरार्चनं नाम
द्व्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्र्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
पञ्चाक्षरादिपूजामन्त्राः
302.m:
And having worshipped Garuḍa outside, one should worship in front of the deity. / Outside the enclosure, with Viṣvaksena and the Lord of Soma in the middle, / having worshipped with Indra and the other attendants, one attains everything.
Thus ends the three hundred and second chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'Worship of the Syllables of the Body'.
Now, the three hundred and third chapter.
The Worship Mantras Beginning with the Five-Syllable Mantra.

303.s:
agnir uvāca
meṣaḥ saṃjñā viṣaṃ sādyamasti dīrghodakaṃ rasaḥ /
etat pañcākṣaraṃ mantraṃ śivadañca śivātmakaṃ //
303.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
मेषः संज्ञा विषं साद्यमस्ति दीर्घोदकं रसः /
एतत् पञ्चाक्षरं मन्त्रं शिवदञ्च शिवात्मकं //
303.m: Agni said: / Meṣa, saṃjñā, viṣa, sādya, asti, the long water [vowel], and rasa: / this five-syllable mantra bestows auspiciousness and is identical with Śiva.

303.s:
tārakādi samabhyarcya devatvādi samāpnuyāt /
jñānātmakaṃ paraṃ brahma paraṃ buddhiḥ śivo hṛdi //
303.d:
तारकादि समभ्यर्च्य देवत्वादि समाप्नुयात् /
ज्ञानात्मकं परं ब्रह्म परं बुद्धिः शिवो हृदि //
303.m: Having worshipped with the praṇava and the rest, one attains godhead and other states. / Supreme Brahman consists of knowledge; supreme intelligence is Śiva in the heart.

303.s:
tacchaktibhūtaḥ sarveśo bhinno brahmādimūrtibhiḥ /
mantrārṇāḥ pañca bhūtāni tanmantrā viṣayās tathā //
303.d:
तच्छक्तिभूतः सर्वेशो भिन्नो ब्रह्मादिमूर्तिभिः /
मन्त्रार्णाः पञ्च भूतानि तन्मन्त्रा विषयास् तथा //
303.m: The Lord of all, consisting of that power, is divided into the forms of Brahmā and the others. / The letters of the mantra are the five elements, and their mantras are the sense-objects;

303.s:
prāṇādivāyavaḥ pañca jñānakarmendriyāṇi ca /
sarvaṃ pañcākṣaraṃ brahma tadvadaṣṭākṣarāntakaḥ //
303.d:
प्राणादिवायवः पञ्च ज्ञानकर्मेन्द्रियाणि च /
सर्वं पञ्चाक्षरं ब्रह्म तद्वदष्टाक्षरान्तकः //
303.m: the five winds beginning with prāṇa, and the organs of sense and action. / Everything is the five-syllable Brahman; likewise is that which ends with the eight syllables.

303.s:
gavyena prakṣayeddīkṣāsthānaṃ mantreṇa coditaṃ /
tantrasambhūtasambhāvaḥ śivamiṣṭvā vidhānataḥ //
:n
1 madhyeṣu toraṇadvahiriti kha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 119
303.d:
गव्येन प्रक्षयेद्दीक्षास्थानं मन्त्रेण चोदितं /
तन्त्रसम्भूतसम्भावः शिवमिष्ट्वा विधानतः //
:न्
1 मध्येषु तोरणद्वहिरिति ख.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 119
303.m:
One should sprinkle the place of initiation with products of the cow as prescribed by the mantra. / Having produced the required state through the Tantra, having worshipped Śiva according to the rules,
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: madhyeṣu toraṇadvahiriti kha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca] [Page 119]

303.s:
mūlamūrtyaṅgavidyābhistaṇḍulakṣepaṇādikam /
kṛtvā caruñca yat kṣīraṃ punastadvibhajet tridhā //
303.d:
मूलमूर्त्यङ्गविद्याभिस्तण्डुलक्षेपणादिकम् /
कृत्वा चरुञ्च यत् क्षीरं पुनस्तद्विभजेत् त्रिधा //
303.m: having performed the scattering of rice and other rites with the root, icon, and limb Vidyās, / and [preparing] the caru and the milk, he should divide it again into three parts.

303.s:
nivedyaikaṃ paraṃ hutvā saśiṣyo 'nyadbhajedguruḥ /
ācamya sakalīkṛtya dadyāccchiṣyāya deśikaḥ //
303.d:
निवेद्यैकं परं हुत्वा सशिष्यो ऽन्यद्भजेद्गुरुः /
आचम्य सकलीकृत्य दद्याच्च्छिष्याय देशिकः //
303.m: Having offered one [part], having made oblations with the other, the teacher with the disciple should consume the remaining one. / Having sipped water and performed the nyāsa of parts, the teacher should give to the disciple

303.s:
dantakāṣṭhaṃ hṛdā japtaṃ kṣīravṛkṣādisambhavam /
saṃśodhya dantān saṃkṣiptvā prajñālyaitat kṣipedbhuvi //
303.d:
दन्तकाष्ठं हृदा जप्तं क्षीरवृक्षादिसम्भवम् /
संशोध्य दन्तान् संक्षिप्त्वा प्रज्ञाल्यैतत् क्षिपेद्भुवि //
303.m: a tooth-stick consecrated with the heart-mantra, obtained from a milky tree or the like. / Having cleaned the teeth, cast it down, and washed it, he should throw it onto the ground.

303.s:
pūrveṇa saumyavārīśagataṃ śubhamatau śubham /
punastaṃ śiṣyamāyāntaṃ(1) śiśvābandhādirakṣitaṃ //
303.d:
पूर्वेण सौम्यवारीशगतं शुभमतौ शुभम् /
पुनस्तं शिष्यमायान्तं(1) शिश्वाबन्धादिरक्षितं //
303.m: Fallen to the east, north, or west, it is auspicious; otherwise, it is inauspicious. / Then, making that arriving disciple protected by the protective tie and other means,

303.s:
kṛtvā vedyāṃ sahānena svapeddarbhāstare budhaḥ /
suṣuptaṃ vīkṣya taṃ śiṣyaḥ prabhāte śrāvayedguruṃ //
303.d:
कृत्वा वेद्यां सहानेन स्वपेद्दर्भास्तरे बुधः /
सुषुप्तं वीक्ष्य तं शिष्यः प्रभाते श्रावयेद्गुरुं //
303.m: the wise [teacher] should sleep with him on an altar covered with darbha grass. / Having seen [the dreams] in deep sleep, the disciple should relate them to the teacher at dawn.

303.s:
śubhaiḥ siddhipadair bhaktistaiḥ punarmaṇḍalārcanam /
maṇḍalaṃ bhadrakādyuktaṃ pūjayetsarvasiddhidaṃ //
303.d:
शुभैः सिद्धिपदैर् भक्तिस्तैः पुनर्मण्डलार्चनम् /
मण्डलं भद्रकाद्युक्तं पूजयेत्सर्वसिद्धिदं //
303.m: If [the dreams] are auspicious and grant success, devotion is generated by them; then comes the worship of the maṇḍala. / One should worship the maṇḍala, such as the bhadraka, which grants all attainments.

303.s:
snātvācamya mṛdā dehaṃ mantrair ālipya kalpyate /
śivatīrthe naraḥ snāyādaghamarṣaṇapūrvakam //
303.d:
स्नात्वाचम्य मृदा देहं मन्त्रैर् आलिप्य कल्प्यते /
शिवतीर्थे नरः स्नायादघमर्षणपूर्वकम् //
303.m: Having bathed, sipped water, and smeared the body with clay with mantras, it is prepared. / A person should bathe in a sacred water of Śiva, preceded by the Aghamarṣaṇa rite.

303.s:
hastābhiṣekaṃ kṛtvātha prāyāt pūjādikaṃ budhaḥ /
mūlenābjāsanaṃ kuryāttena pūrakakumbhakān //
303.d:
हस्ताभिषेकं कृत्वाथ प्रायात् पूजादिकं बुधः /
मूलेनाब्जासनं कुर्यात्तेन पूरककुम्भकान् //
303.m: Having then consecrated his hands, the wise one should proceed to worship and other rites. / He should form the lotus seat with the root-mantra, and with it perform inhalation and retention [of breath].

303.s:
ātmānaṃ yojayitvordhvaṃ śikhānte dvādaśāṅgule /
saṃśoṣya dagdhvā svatanuṃ plāvayedamṛtena ca //
303.d:
आत्मानं योजयित्वोर्ध्वं शिखान्ते द्वादशाङ्गुले /
संशोष्य दग्ध्वा स्वतनुं प्लावयेदमृतेन च //
303.m: Having united the self above, at the end of the tuft of hair twelve finger-widths [up], / having dried up and burned his own body, he should flood it with nectar.

303.s:
dhmātvā divyaṃ vapustasminnātmānañca punarnayet /
kṛtvevaṃ cātmaśuddhiḥ syādvinyasyārcanamārabhet //
303.d:
ध्मात्वा दिव्यं वपुस्तस्मिन्नात्मानञ्च पुनर्नयेत् /
कृत्वेवं चात्मशुद्धिः स्याद्विन्यस्यार्चनमारभेत् //
303.m: Having meditated upon a divine body, he should bring the self back into it. / Having thus performed the purification of self, and having deposited [the mantras], he should begin worship.

303.s:
kramāt kṛṣṇasitaśyāmaraktapītā nagādayaḥ /
mantrārṇā daṇḍināṅgāni teṣu sarvāstu mūrtayaḥ //
:n
1 śiṣyamācāntamiti ña..
:p 120
303.d:
क्रमात् कृष्णसितश्यामरक्तपीता नगादयः /
मन्त्रार्णा दण्डिनाङ्गानि तेषु सर्वास्तु मूर्तयः //
:न्
1 शिष्यमाचान्तमिति ञ..
:प् 120
303.m:
Sequentially black, white, dark, red, and yellow are the mountains and other deities; / the syllables of the mantra are the body parts of the staff-bearer, and all forms dwell in them.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: śiṣyamācāntamiti ña..] [Page 120]

303.s:
aṅguṣṭhādikaniṣṭhāntaṃ vinyasyāṅgāni sarvataḥ /
nyasenmantrākṣaraṃ pādaguhyahṛdvaktramūrdhasu //
303.d:
अङ्गुष्ठादिकनिष्ठान्तं विन्यस्याङ्गानि सर्वतः /
न्यसेन्मन्त्राक्षरं पादगुह्यहृद्वक्त्रमूर्धसु //
303.m: Having assigned [the syllables to] the limbs everywhere, from the thumb to the little finger, / one should deposit the syllables of the mantra on the feet, the private parts, the heart, the mouth, and the head.

303.s:
vyāpakaṃ nyasya mūrdhādi mūlamaṅgāni vinyaset /
raktapītaśyāmasitān pīṭhapādān svakālajān //
303.d:
व्यापकं न्यस्य मूर्धादि मूलमङ्गानि विन्यसेत् /
रक्तपीतश्यामसितान् पीठपादान् स्वकालजान् //
303.m: Having performed the pervasive ritual deposition from the head downwards, one should deposit the root [mantra] and the limbs. / The red, yellow, dark, and white legs of the pedestal, born of their respective times,

303.s:
svāṅgānmantrair nyasedgātrāṇyadharmādīni dikṣu ca /
tatra padmañca suryādimaṇḍale tritayaṃ guṇān //
303.d:
स्वाङ्गान्मन्त्रैर् न्यसेद्गात्राण्यधर्मादीनि दिक्षु च /
तत्र पद्मञ्च सुर्यादिमण्डले त्रितयं गुणान् //
303.m: and the members [of the pedestal]—unrighteousness and the rest—he should deposit from his own limbs with mantras in the cardinal directions. / There [on the pedestal he should deposit] the lotus, and in the disc of the sun and the others, the triad of qualities.

303.s:
pūrvādipatre kāmādyā navakaṃ karṇikopari /
vāmā jyeṣṭhā kramādraudro kālī kalavikāriṇī //
303.d:
पूर्वादिपत्रे कामाद्या नवकं कर्णिकोपरि /
वामा ज्येष्ठा क्रमाद्रौद्रो काली कलविकारिणी //
303.m: On the petals beginning in the east, the [śaktis] beginning with Vāmā, and a group of nine on the pericarp: / Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and in order Raudrī, Kālī, Kalavikāriṇī,

303.s:
balavikāriṇī cārtha balapramathanī tathā /
sarvabhūtadamanī ca navamī ca manonmanī //
303.d:
बलविकारिणी चार्थ बलप्रमथनी तथा /
सर्वभूतदमनी च नवमी च मनोन्मनी //
303.m: and Balavikāriṇī, Balapramathanī, / and Sarvabhūtadamanī, and the ninth, Manonmanī.

303.s:
śvetā raktā sitā pītā śyāmā vahninibhāṣitā /
kṛṣṇāruṇāś ca tāḥ śaktīrjvālārūpāḥ smaret kramāt //
303.d:
श्वेता रक्ता सिता पीता श्यामा वह्निनिभाषिता /
कृष्णारुणाश् च ताः शक्तीर्ज्वालारूपाः स्मरेत् क्रमात् //
303.m: White, red, white, yellow, dark, flame-colored, / black, and reddish-brown—one should visualize those powers in order, in the form of flames.

303.s:
anantayogapīṭhāya āvāhyātha hṛdabjataḥ /
sphaṭikābhaṃ caturvāhuṃ phalaśūladharaṃ śivam //
303.d:
अनन्तयोगपीठाय आवाह्याथ हृदब्जतः /
स्फटिकाभं चतुर्वाहुं फलशूलधरं शिवम् //
303.m: Having invoked [Śiva] for the seat of infinite yoga from the lotus of the heart, / [one should visualize] Śiva, radiant as crystal, four-armed, holding a fruit and a trident,

303.s:
sābhayaṃ varadaṃ pañcavadaṃnañca trilocanam /
patreṣu murtayaḥ pañca sthāpyāstatpuruṣādayaḥ //
303.d:
साभयं वरदं पञ्चवदंनञ्च त्रिलोचनम् /
पत्रेषु मुर्तयः पञ्च स्थाप्यास्तत्पुरुषादयः //
303.m: granting fearlessness and boons, five-faced, and three-eyed. / On the petals, the five icons beginning with Tatpuruṣa are to be placed.

303.s:
pūrve tatpuruṣaḥ śveto aghoro 'ṣṭabhujo 'sitāḥ /
caturvāhumukhaḥ pītāḥ sadyojātaś ca paścime //
303.d:
पूर्वे तत्पुरुषः श्वेतो अघोरो ऽष्टभुजो ऽसिताः /
चतुर्वाहुमुखः पीताः सद्योजातश् च पश्चिमे //
303.m: In the east is Tatpuruṣa, white; Aghora is eight-armed and dark; / Sadyojāta in the west is four-armed, four-faced, and yellow.

303.s:
vāmadevaḥ strīvilāsī caturvaktrabhujo 'ruṇaḥ /
saumye pañcāsya īśāne īśānaḥ sarvadaḥ sitaḥ //
303.d:
वामदेवः स्त्रीविलासी चतुर्वक्त्रभुजो ऽरुणः /
सौम्ये पञ्चास्य ईशाने ईशानः सर्वदः सितः //
303.m: Vāmadeva is sportive with women, four-faced, four-armed, and reddish; / in the north is the five-faced [form], and in the northeast is Īśāna, all-bestowing and white.

303.s:
iṣṭāṅgāni yathānyāyamanantaṃ sūkṣmamarcayet /
siddheśvaraṃ tvekanetraṃ pūrvādau diśa pūjayet //
303.d:
इष्टाङ्गानि यथान्यायमनन्तं सूक्ष्ममर्चयेत् /
सिद्धेश्वरं त्वेकनेत्रं पूर्वादौ दिश पूजयेत् //
303.m: One should worship the desired limbs according to rule, and Ananta and Sūkṣma; / in the cardinal directions beginning with the east, one should worship Siddheśvara and Ekanetra,

303.s:
ekarudraṃ trinetrañca śrīkaṇṭhañca śikhaṇḍinam /
:p 121
aiśānyādividikṣvete vidyeśāḥ kamalāsanāḥ(1) //
303.d:
एकरुद्रं त्रिनेत्रञ्च श्रीकण्ठञ्च शिखण्डिनम् /
:प् 121
ऐशान्यादिविदिक्ष्वेते विद्येशाः कमलासनाः(1) //

303.s:
śvetaḥ pītaḥ sito rakto dhūmro rakto 'ruṇaḥ śitaḥ /
śūlāśaniśareśvāsavāhavaś caturānanāḥ //
303.d:
श्वेतः पीतः सितो रक्तो धूम्रो रक्तो ऽरुणः शितः /
शूलाशनिशरेश्वासवाहवश् चतुराननाः //
303.m: White, yellow, white, red, smoke-colored, red, reddish-brown, and white; / their arms bear a trident, a thunderbolt, and a bow and arrow, and they are four-faced.

303.s:
umā vaṇḍeśanandīśau mahākālo gaṇeśvaraḥ /
vṛṣo bhṛṅgariṭiskandānuttarādau prapūjayet //
303.d:
उमा वण्डेशनन्दीशौ महाकालो गणेश्वरः /
वृषो भृङ्गरिटिस्कन्दानुत्तरादौ प्रपूजयेत् //
303.m: One should worship Umā, Caṇḍeśa and Nandīśa, Mahākāla, Gaṇeśa, / the Bull, Bhṛṅgiriṭi, and Skanda, beginning in the north.

303.s:
kuliśaṃ śaktidaṇḍau ca khaḍgapāśadhvajau gadāṃ /
śūlaṃ cakraṃ yajet padmaṃ pūvvādau devamarcya ca //
303.d:
कुलिशं शक्तिदण्डौ च खड्गपाशध्वजौ गदां /
शूलं चक्रं यजेत् पद्मं पूव्वादौ देवमर्च्य च //
303.m: One should worship the thunderbolt, the spear and the staff, the sword, the noose, the banner, the mace, / the trident, the discus, and the lotus, beginning in the east, having worshipped the god.

303.s:
tato 'dhivāsitaṃ śiṣyaṃ pāyayedgavyapañcakam /
ācāntaṃ prokṣye netrāntair netre netreṇa bandhayet //
303.d:
ततो ऽधिवासितं शिष्यं पाययेद्गव्यपञ्चकम् /
आचान्तं प्रोक्ष्ये नेत्रान्तैर् नेत्रे नेत्रेण बन्धयेत् //
303.m: Then one should have the pupil, who has undergone preliminary consecration, drink the five products of the cow. / Having rinsed his mouth and sprinkled him [with water] with the eye [mantras], one should blindfold his eyes with the eye [mantra].

303.s:
dvāraṃ praveśayecchipyaṃ maṇḍapasyātha dakṣiṇe /
sāsanādikuśāsīnaṃ tatra saṃśodhayedguruḥ //
303.d:
द्वारं प्रवेशयेच्छिप्यं मण्डपस्याथ दक्षिणे /
सासनादिकुशासीनं तत्र संशोधयेद्गुरुः //
303.m: He should lead the pupil through the door in the south of the pavilion; / seated there on kuśa grass with a seat and the like, the guru should purify him.

303.s:
āditattvāni saṃhṛtya paramārthe layaḥ kramāt /
punarutpādayecchiṣyaṃ sṛṣṭimārgeṇa deśikaḥ //
303.d:
आदितत्त्वानि संहृत्य परमार्थे लयः क्रमात् /
पुनरुत्पादयेच्छिष्यं सृष्टिमार्गेण देशिकः //
303.m: Having dissolved the primary cosmic principles in order into the supreme reality, / the teacher should generate the pupil again by the process of creation.

303.s:
nyāsaṃ śiṣye tataḥ kṛtvā taṃ pradakṣiṇamānayet /
paścimadvāramānīya kṣepayet kusumāñjalim //
303.d:
न्यासं शिष्ये ततः कृत्वा तं प्रदक्षिणमानयेत् /
पश्चिमद्वारमानीय क्षेपयेत् कुसुमाञ्जलिम् //
303.m: Then, having performed the ritual deposition upon the pupil, he should lead him in a clockwise circumambulation; / having brought him to the western door, he should have him throw a handful of flowers.

303.s:
yasmin patanti puṣpāṇi tannāmādyaṃ vinirdiśet /
pārśveyāgabhuvaḥ khāte kuṇḍe sannabhimekhale(2) //
303.d:
यस्मिन् पतन्ति पुष्पाणि तन्नामाद्यं विनिर्दिशेत् /
पार्श्वेयागभुवः खाते कुण्डे सन्नभिमेखले(2) //
303.m: Upon whatever [deity] the flowers fall, he should assign him that name as the primary one. / In the fire-pit dug beside the sacrificial ground, possessing a proper navel and girdles,

303.s:
śivāgniṃ janayitveṣṭvā punaḥ śiṣyeṇa cārcayet /
dhyānenātmanibhaṃ śiṣyaṃ saṃhṛtya pralayaḥ kramāt //
303.d:
शिवाग्निं जनयित्वेष्ट्वा पुनः शिष्येण चार्चयेत् /
ध्यानेनात्मनिभं शिष्यं संहृत्य प्रलयः क्रमात् //
303.m: having generated the Śiva-fire and sacrificed, he should have him worship again with the pupil. / Having brought the pupil, who resembles oneself, through meditation into gradual dissolution,

303.s:
punarutpādya tatpāṇau dadyāddarbhāṃś ca mantritān /
pṛthivyādīni tattvāni juhuyāddhṛdayādibhiḥ //
:n
1 kamalānanā iti ña..
2 sandhādimekhale iti kha..
:p 122
303.d:
पुनरुत्पाद्य तत्पाणौ दद्याद्दर्भांश् च मन्त्रितान् /
पृथिव्यादीनि तत्त्वानि जुहुयाद्धृदयादिभिः //
:न्
1 कमलानना इति ञ..
2 सन्धादिमेखले इति ख..
:प् 122
303.m:
and having generated him again, he should place consecrated darbha grass in his hand. / He should make oblations of the cosmic principles beginning with earth using the heart and other [mantras].
[Footnote]
1 [Variant] "kamalānanāḥ" according to manuscript ña.
2 [Variant] "sandhādimekhale" according to manuscript kha. / [Page 122]

303.s:
ekaikasya śataṃ hutvā vyomamūlena homayet /
hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ kuryādastreṇāṣṭāhutīrhunet //
303.d:
एकैकस्य शतं हुत्वा व्योममूलेन होमयेत् /
हुत्वा पूर्णाहुतिं कुर्यादस्त्रेणाष्टाहुतीर्हुनेत् //
303.m: Having offered a hundred oblations for each one, he should offer fire oblations with the root [mantra] of ether. / Having made the fire oblations, he should make the full oblation; he should offer eight fire oblations with the weapon [mantra].

303.s:
prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhyarthaṃ tataḥ śeṣaṃ samāpayet /
kumbhaṃ samantritaṃ prārcya śiśuṃ pīṭhe 'bhiṣecayet //
303.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं विशुद्ध्यर्थं ततः शेषं समापयेत् /
कुम्भं समन्त्रितं प्रार्च्य शिशुं पीठे ऽभिषेचयेत् //
303.m: An expiation for the sake of complete purity, and then he should finish the remainder. / Having worshipped the jar that has been consecrated with mantras, he should consecrate the youth on the pedestal with aspersion.

303.s:
śiṣye tu samayaṃ datvā svarṇādyaiḥ svaguruṃ yajet /
dīkṣā pañcākṣarasyoktā viṣṇvāderevameva hi //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe pañcākṣarādipūjāmantrā nāma
tryadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha caturadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
pañcapañcāśadviṣṇunāmāṇi
303.d:
शिष्ये तु समयं दत्वा स्वर्णाद्यैः स्वगुरुं यजेत् /
दीक्षा पञ्चाक्षरस्योक्ता विष्ण्वादेरेवमेव हि //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पञ्चाक्षरादिपूजामन्त्रा नाम
त्र्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुरधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
पञ्चपञ्चाशद्विष्णुनामाणि
303.m:
Having imparted the rule of conduct to the pupil, he should worship his guru with gold and other gifts. / The initiation of the five-syllable mantra has been spoken; in this very manner is that of Viṣṇu and the other deities.
Thus ends the three hundred and third chapter, entitled “The Worship Mantras of the Five-Syllable [Formula] and Others,” in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and fourth chapter.
The Fifty-Five Names of Viṣṇu.

304.s:
agnir uvāca
japan vai pañcapañcāśadviṣṇunāmāni yo naraḥ /
mantrajapyādiphalabhāk tīrtheṣvarcādi cākṣayam //
304.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
जपन् वै पञ्चपञ्चाशद्विष्णुनामानि यो नरः /
मन्त्रजप्यादिफलभाक् तीर्थेष्वर्चादि चाक्षयम् //
304.m:
Agni said:
The man who recites the fifty-five names of Viṣṇu
obtains the fruit of mantra recitation and the rest, and imperishable [merit] from worship and other rites at sacred fords.

304.s:
puṣkare puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ gayāyāñca gadādharam /
rāghavañcitrakūṭe tu prabhāse daityasūdanam //
304.d:
पुष्करे पुण्डरीकाक्षं गयायाञ्च गदाधरम् /
राघवञ्चित्रकूटे तु प्रभासे दैत्यसूदनम् //
304.m: [One should know] Puṇḍarīkākṣa at Puṣkara, and Gadādhara at Gayā, / Rāghava at Citrakūṭa, and the Slayer of Daityas at Prabhāsa,

304.s:
jayaṃ jayantyāṃ tadvacca jayantaṃ hastināpure /
vārāhaṃ vardhamāne ca kāśmīre cakrapāṇinam //
304.d:
जयं जयन्त्यां तद्वच्च जयन्तं हस्तिनापुरे /
वाराहं वर्धमाने च काश्मीरे चक्रपाणिनम् //
304.m: Jaya at Jayantī, and likewise Jayanta at Hastināpura, / Vārāha at Vardhamāna, and Cakrapāṇi in Kaśmīr,

304.s:
janārdanañca kubjāmre mathurāyāñca keśavam /
kubjāmrake hṛṣīkeśaṃ gaṅgādvāre jaṭādharam //
304.d:
जनार्दनञ्च कुब्जाम्रे मथुरायाञ्च केशवम् /
कुब्जाम्रके हृषीकेशं गङ्गाद्वारे जटाधरम् //
304.m: Janārdana at Kubjāmra, and Keśava at Mathurā, / Hṛṣīkeśa at Kubjāmraka, and Jaṭādhara at Gaṅgādvāra,

304.s:
śālagrāme mahāyogaṃ hariṃ gobardhanācale /
:p 123
piṇḍārake caturvāhuṃ śaṅkhoddhāre ca śaṅkhinam //
304.d:
शालग्रामे महायोगं हरिं गोबर्धनाचले /
:प् 123
पिण्डारके चतुर्वाहुं शङ्खोद्धारे च शङ्खिनम् //
304.m:
Mahāyoga at Śālagrāma, Hari on Mount Govardhana,
[Page 123]
the Four-Armed at Piṇḍāraka, and the Conch-Bearer at Śaṅkhoddhāra,

304.s:
vāmanañca kurukṣetre yamunāyāṃ trivikramam /
viśveśvaraṃ tathā śoṇe kapilaṃ pūrvasāgare //
304.d:
वामनञ्च कुरुक्षेत्रे यमुनायां त्रिविक्रमम् /
विश्वेश्वरं तथा शोणे कपिलं पूर्वसागरे //
304.m: Vāmana at Kurukṣetra, and Trivikrama on the Yamunā, / Viśveśvara on the Śoṇa, Kapila at the Eastern Ocean,

304.s:
viṣṇuṃ mahodadhau vidyādgaṅgāsāgarasaṅgame /
vanamālañca kiṣkindhyāṃ devaṃ raivatakaṃ viduḥ //
304.d:
विष्णुं महोदधौ विद्याद्गङ्गासागरसङ्गमे /
वनमालञ्च किष्किन्ध्यां देवं रैवतकं विदुः //
304.m: one should know Viṣṇu in the Great Ocean, at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, / Vanamālin at Kiṣkindhā, and the god at Raivataka is known [by wise men],

304.s:
kāśītaṭe mahāyogaṃ virajāyāṃ ripuñjayam /
viśākhayūpe hy ajitannepāle lokabhāvanam //
304.d:
काशीतटे महायोगं विरजायां रिपुञ्जयम् /
विशाखयूपे ह्य् अजितन्नेपाले लोकभावनम् //
304.m: Mahāyoga on the bank of Kāśī, Ripuñjaya at Virajā, / Ajita at Viśākhayūpa, and Lokabhāvana in Nepāla.

304.s:
dvārakāyāṃ viddhi kṛṣṇaṃ mandare madhusūdanam /
lokākule ripuharaṃ śālagrāme hariṃ smaret //
304.d:
द्वारकायां विद्धि कृष्णं मन्दरे मधुसूदनम् /
लोकाकुले रिपुहरं शालग्रामे हरिं स्मरेत् //
304.m: Know Kṛṣṇa at Dvārakā, Madhusūdana at Mandara, / Ripuhara at Lokākula, and one should remember Hari at Śālagrāma.

304.s:
puruṣaṃ pūruṣavaṭe vimale ca jagatprabhuṃ /
anantaṃ saindhavāraṇye daṇḍake śārṅgadhāriṇam //
304.d:
पुरुषं पूरुषवटे विमले च जगत्प्रभुं /
अनन्तं सैन्धवारण्ये दण्डके शार्ङ्गधारिणम् //
304.m: Puruṣa at Pūruṣavaṭa, and the Lord of the Universe at Vimala, / Ananta in the Saindhava Forest, and the Bow-Holder in Daṇḍaka,

304.s:
utpalāvartake śaurīṃ narmadāyāṃ śriyaḥ patiṃ /
dāmodaraṃ raivatake nandāyāṃ jalaśāyinaṃ //
304.d:
उत्पलावर्तके शौरीं नर्मदायां श्रियः पतिं /
दामोदरं रैवतके नन्दायां जलशायिनं //
304.m: Śauri at Utpalāvartaka, the Husband of Śrī on the Narmadā, / Dāmodara at Raivataka, and the Recliner on the Water at Nandā,

304.s:
gopīśvarañca sindhvavdhau māhendre cācyutaṃ viṭuḥ /
sahādrau devadeveśaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ māgadhe vane //
304.d:
गोपीश्वरञ्च सिन्ध्वव्धौ माहेन्द्रे चाच्युतं विटुः /
सहाद्रौ देवदेवेशं वैकुण्ठं मागधे वने //
304.m: and Gopīśvara in the ocean of the Sindhu, and they know Acyuta at Mahendra, / the Lord of the God of Gods on Mount Sahya, and Vaikuṇṭha in the Māgadha forest,

304.s:
sarvapāpaharaṃ vindhye auḍre tu puruṣottamam /
ātmānaṃ hṛdaye viddhi japatāṃ bhuktimuktidam //
304.d:
सर्वपापहरं विन्ध्ये औड्रे तु पुरुषोत्तमम् /
आत्मानं हृदये विद्धि जपतां भुक्तिमुक्तिदम् //
304.m: the Destroyer of All Sins in the Vindhya, and Puruṣottama in Oḍra; / know the Self in the heart, bestowing worldly enjoyment and liberation upon those who recite [His names].

304.s:
vaṭe vaṭe vaiśravaṇaṃ catvare catvare śivam /
parvate parvate rāmaṃ sarvatra madhusūdanaṃ //
304.d:
वटे वटे वैश्रवणं चत्वरे चत्वरे शिवम् /
पर्वते पर्वते रामं सर्वत्र मधुसूदनं //
304.m: Vaiśravaṇa under every banyan tree, Śiva at every crossroads, / Rāma on every mountain, and Madhusūdana everywhere;

304.s:
naraṃ bhūmau tathā vyomni vaśiṣṭhe garuḍadhvajam /
vāsudevañca sarvatra saṃsmaran bhuktimuktibhāk //
304.d:
नरं भूमौ तथा व्योम्नि वशिष्ठे गरुडध्वजम् /
वासुदेवञ्च सर्वत्र संस्मरन् भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् //
304.m: Nara on the earth, likewise in the sky, and Garuda-Bannered at the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha; / constantly remembering Vāsudeva everywhere, one shares in worldly enjoyment and liberation.

304.s:
nāmānyetāni viṣṇīś ca japtvā sarvamavāpnuyāt /
kṣetreṣveteṣu yat śrāddhaṃ dānaṃ japyañca tarpaṇam //
:p 124
304.d:
नामान्येतानि विष्णीश् च जप्त्वा सर्वमवाप्नुयात् /
क्षेत्रेष्वेतेषु यत् श्राद्धं दानं जप्यञ्च तर्पणम् //
:प् 124
304.m:
Having recited these names of Viṣṇu, one obtains everything. / Whatever ancestral rite, gift, recitation, and water libation is done in these sacred fields,
[Page 124]

304.s:
tatsarvaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ mṛto brahmamayo bhavet /
yaḥ paṭhet śṛṇuyādvāpi nirmalaḥ svargamāpnuyāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe pañcapañcāśadviṣṇunāmāni nāma
caturadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nārasiṃhādimantrāḥ
304.d:
तत्सर्वं कोटिगुणितं मृतो ब्रह्ममयो भवेत् /
यः पठेत् शृणुयाद्वापि निर्मलः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पञ्चपञ्चाशद्विष्णुनामानि नाम
चतुरधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चाधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
नारसिंहादिमन्त्राः
304.m:
all that is multiplied ten-millionfold; when dead, one becomes identified with Brahman. / Whoever recites or even listens to [them], becoming free of stain, reaches heaven.
Thus ends the three hundred and fourth chapter, entitled “The Fifty-Five Names of Viṣṇu,” in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and fifth chapter.
The Mantras of Narasiṃha and Others.

305.s:
agnir uvāca
stambho vidveṣaṇoccāṭa utsādo bhramamāraṇe /
vyādhiśceti smṛtaṃ kṣutraṃ tanmokṣo vakṣyate śṛṇu //
oṃ namo bhagavate unmattarudrāya bhrama 2 bhrāmaya 2 amukaṃ vitrāsaya
udbhrāmaya 2 raudreṇa rūpeṇa hūṃ phaṭh ṭha 2
305.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
स्तम्भो विद्वेषणोच्चाट उत्सादो भ्रममारणे /
व्याधिश्चेति स्मृतं क्षुत्रं तन्मोक्षो वक्ष्यते शृणु //
ओं नमो भगवते उन्मत्तरुद्राय भ्रम 2 भ्रामय 2 अमुकं वित्रासय
उद्भ्रामय 2 रौद्रेण रूपेण हूं फठ् ठ 2
305.m:
Agni said: / Immobilization, sowing hatred, eradication, ruin, delusion, killing, / and disease—these are remembered as the cruel [sorceries]; liberation from them will be spoken, listen!
Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lord, the Frenzied Rudra! Wander, wander! Make wander, make wander! Terrify such-and-such person! / Agitate, agitate with your terrible form! Hūṃ phaṭ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ!

305.s:
śmaśāne niśi japtena trilakṣaṃ madhunā hunet /
citāgnau dhūrtasamidubhirbhrāmyate satataṃ ripuḥ //
305.d:
श्मशाने निशि जप्तेन त्रिलक्षं मधुना हुनेत् /
चिताग्नौ धूर्तसमिदुभिर्भ्राम्यते सततं रिपुः //
305.m: Recited at night in a cremation ground, one should make three hundred thousand oblations with honey / in the fire of a funeral pyre with firewood of thorn-apple; the enemy is perpetually driven mad.

305.s:
hemagairikayā kṛṣṇā pratimā haimasūcibhiḥ /
japtvā vidhyecca tatkaṇṭhe hṛdi vā miyate ripuḥ //
305.d:
हेमगैरिकया कृष्णा प्रतिमा हैमसूचिभिः /
जप्त्वा विध्येच्च तत्कण्ठे हृदि वा मियते रिपुः //
305.m: A black doll [fashioned] with yellow ochre, pierced with golden needles / in its neck or in its heart after reciting [the mantra], the enemy dies.

305.s:
kharabālacitābhasma brahmadaṇḍī ca markaṭī /
gṛhe vā mūrdhni taccūrṇaṃ japtamutsādakṛta kṣipet //
305.d:
खरबालचिताभस्म ब्रह्मदण्डी च मर्कटी /
गृहे वा मूर्ध्नि तच्चूर्णं जप्तमुत्सादकृत क्षिपेत् //
305.m: The hair of a donkey, ashes from a funeral pyre, *brahmadaṇḍī*, and cowhage; / one should throw that recited-over powder in the house or on the head, causing ruin.

305.s:
bhṛgvākāśau sadīptāgnirbhṛgurvahniś ca varma phaṭ /
evaṃ sahasrāre hūṃ phaṭ ācakrāya svāhā hṛdayaṃ vicakrāya
śivaḥ
śikhācakrāyātha kavacaṃ vicakrāyātha netrakam //
:p 125
305.d:
भृग्वाकाशौ सदीप्ताग्निर्भृगुर्वह्निश् च वर्म फट् /
एवं सहस्रारे हूं फट् आचक्राय स्वाहा हृदयं विचक्राय
शिवः
शिखाचक्रायाथ कवचं विचक्रायाथ नेत्रकम् //
:प् 125

305.s:
sañcakrāyāstramudiṣṭaṃ jyālācakrāya pūrvavat /
śārṅgaṃ sudarśanaṃ kṣudragrahahṛt sarvasādhanam //
305.d:
सञ्चक्रायास्त्रमुदिष्टं ज्यालाचक्राय पूर्ववत् /
शार्ङ्गं सुदर्शनं क्षुद्रग्रहहृत् सर्वसाधनम् //
305.m: *sañcakrāya* is prescribed for the weapon; *jvālācakrāya* as before. / The bow Śārṅga and Sudarśana remove evil spirits and are the means to all attainments.

305.s:
mūrdhākṣimukhahṛdguhyapāde hy asyākṣarānnyaset /
cakrābjāsanamagnyābhaṃ daṃṣṭraṇañca caturbhujam //
305.d:
मूर्धाक्षिमुखहृद्गुह्यपादे ह्य् अस्याक्षरान्न्यसेत् /
चक्राब्जासनमग्न्याभं दंष्ट्रणञ्च चतुर्भुजम् //
305.m: One should ritually deposit its syllables on the crown of the head, eyes, mouth, heart, private parts, and feet. / [One should visualize the deity] seated on a lotus upon a discus, shining like fire, having fangs, and four-armed,
holding conch, discus, mace, lotus, dart, and elephant goad in hand, / bearing a bow, with tawny hair and eyes, whose spokes pervade the three worlds.

305.s:
nābhistenāgninā viddhā naśyante vyādhayo grahāḥ /
pītañcakraṃ gadā raktāḥ svarāḥ śyāmamavāntaraṃ //
305.d:
नाभिस्तेनाग्निना विद्धा नश्यन्ते व्याधयो ग्रहाः /
पीतञ्चक्रं गदा रक्ताः स्वराः श्याममवान्तरं //
305.m: Pierced by that fire in the navel, diseases and seizing spirits are destroyed. / The discus is yellow, the maces are red, the vowels [are in] the dark intermediate space;

305.s:
nemiḥ śvetā vahiḥ kṛṣṇavarṇarekhā ca pārthivī /
madhyetaremare varṇānevaṃ cakradvayaṃ(1) likhet //
305.d:
नेमिः श्वेता वहिः कृष्णवर्णरेखा च पार्थिवी /
मध्येतरेमरे वर्णानेवं चक्रद्वयं(1) लिखेत् //
305.m: the rim is white, and the outer line is earth-colored, black. / In the middle and on the spokes one should write the syllables; in this way one should draw the two wheels.

305.s:
ādāvānīya kumbhodaṃ gocare sannidhāya ca /
dattvā sudarśanaṃ tatra yāmye cakre hunet kramāt //
305.d:
आदावानीय कुम्भोदं गोचरे सन्निधाय च /
दत्त्वा सुदर्शनं तत्र याम्ये चक्रे हुनेत् क्रमात् //
305.m: First having brought water in a pot and placed it within sight, / and having invoked Sudarśana there, one should make fire oblations sequentially in the southern wheel:

305.s:
ājyāpāmārgasamidho hy akṣataṃ tilasarṣapau /
pāyasaṃ gavyamājyañca sahasrāṣṭakasaṃkhyayā //
305.d:
आज्यापामार्गसमिधो ह्य् अक्षतं तिलसर्षपौ /
पायसं गव्यमाज्यञ्च सहस्राष्टकसंख्यया //
305.m: ghee, firewood of *apāmārga*, unhusked barley grains, sesamum and mustard seeds, / milk-rice, bovine products, and ghee, to the count of eight thousand.

305.s:
hutaśeṣaṃ kṣiptet kumbhe pratidravyaṃ vidhānavit /
prasthānena kṛtaṃ piṇḍaṃ kumbhe tasminniveśayet //
305.d:
हुतशेषं क्षिप्तेत् कुम्भे प्रतिद्रव्यं विधानवित् /
प्रस्थानेन कृतं पिण्डं कुम्भे तस्मिन्निवेशयेत् //
305.m: One knowing the rite should cast the remainder of the oblation into the pot for each substance. / One should place a rice-ball made of a measure of a *prastha* into that pot.

305.s:
viṣṇādi sarvaṃ tatraiva nyaset tatraiva dakṣiṇe /
namo viṣṇujanebhyaḥ sarvaśāntikarebhyaḥ pratigṛhṇantu
śāntaye namaḥ
dadyādanena mantreṇa hutaśeṣāmbhasā baliṃ //
305.d:
विष्णादि सर्वं तत्रैव न्यसेत् तत्रैव दक्षिणे /
नमो विष्णुजनेभ्यः सर्वशान्तिकरेभ्यः प्रतिगृह्णन्तु
शान्तये नमः
दद्यादनेन मन्त्रेण हुतशेषाम्भसा बलिं //
305.m:
One should ritually deposit everything, Viṣṇu and the rest, right there; right there to the south,
"Obeisance to the attendants of Viṣṇu who pacify all things; may they accept this; obeisance for peace."
With this mantra one should give a food-offering with the water left over from the fire oblation.

305.s:
phalake kalpite pātre palāśaṃ kṣīraśākhinaḥ /
gavyapūrṇe niveśyaiva dikṣvevaṃ homayeddvijaiḥ //
305.d:
फलके कल्पिते पात्रे पलाशं क्षीरशाखिनः /
गव्यपूर्णे निवेश्यैव दिक्ष्वेवं होमयेद्द्विजैः //
305.m: Having placed a palāśa [leaf] of a milk-exuding tree in a vessel prepared on a board / filled with bovine products, one should have fire oblations made in the cardinal directions by Brahmins.

305.s:
sadakṣiṇamidaṃ homadvayaṃ bhūtādināśanam /
:n
1 varṇadvayamiti kha..
:p 126
gavyāktapatralikhitair niṣparṇaiḥ kṣudramuddhṛtam //
305.d:
सदक्षिणमिदं होमद्वयं भूतादिनाशनम् /
:न्
1 वर्णद्वयमिति ख..
:प् 126
गव्याक्तपत्रलिखितैर् निष्पर्णैः क्षुद्रमुद्धृतम् //
305.m:
Accompanied by a sacrificial fee, this pair of fire oblations destroys spirits and other [harmful beings].
[Footnote mark]
1. Variant reading: *varṇadvayam* in manuscript *kha*.
[Page 126]
Sorcery is eradicated by leafless twigs written [with mantras] smeared with bovine products.

305.s:
dūrvābhirāyuṣe padmaiḥ śriye putrā uḍugbaraiḥ /
gosiddhyai sarpiṣā goṣṭhe medhāyai sarvaśākhinā //
oṃ kṣauṃ namo bhagavate nārasiṃhāya jvālāmāline
dīptadaṃṣṭrāyāgninetrāya sarvarakṣoghnāya
sarvabhūtavināśāya sarvajvaravināśāya daha 2 paca 2 rakṣa 2 hūṃ
phaṭ
305.d:
दूर्वाभिरायुषे पद्मैः श्रिये पुत्रा उडुग्बरैः /
गोसिद्ध्यै सर्पिषा गोष्ठे मेधायै सर्वशाखिना //
ओं क्षौं नमो भगवते नारसिंहाय ज्वालामालिने
दीप्तदंष्ट्रायाग्निनेत्राय सर्वरक्षोघ्नाय
सर्वभूतविनाशाय सर्वज्वरविनाशाय दह 2 पच 2 रक्ष 2 हूं
फट्
305.m:
[Fire oblations] with dūrvā grass are for long life; with lotuses, for fortune; with *udumbara* wood, for sons; / with ghee in a cowshed, for success with cattle; with all milk-trees, for wisdom.
Om kṣauṃ. Obeisance to the Blessed Lord, to Nārasiṃha, who wears a garland of flames, / who has blazing fangs, who has eyes of fire, who slays all demons, / who destroys all evil spirits, who cures all fevers; burn, burn; cook, cook; protect, protect; *hūṃ phaṭ*.

305.s:
mantroyaṃ nārasiṃhasya makalāghnivāraṇaḥ /
japyādinā haret kṣudragrahamārīviṣāmayān /
cūrṇamaṇḍūkavayasā jalāgnistambhakṛdbhavet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nārasiṃhādimantrā nāma
pañcādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha ṣaṣṭhādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
trailokyamohanamantrāḥ
305.d:
मन्त्रोयं नारसिंहस्य मकलाघ्निवारणः /
जप्यादिना हरेत् क्षुद्रग्रहमारीविषामयान् /
चूर्णमण्डूकवयसा जलाग्निस्तम्भकृद्भवेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नारसिंहादिमन्त्रा नाम
पञ्चाधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ षष्ठाधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
त्रैलोक्यमोहनमन्त्राः
305.m:
This mantra of Nārasiṃha averts all troubles. / Through recitation and the like it removes sorcery, seizing spirits, pestilence, poisons, and ailments. / With powder and the bile of a frog, it produces paralysis of water and fire.
Thus ends the three hundred and fifth chapter, titled "Mantras of Nārasiṃha and Others," in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now the three hundred and sixth chapter.
[The Trailokyamohana Mantras]

306.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वक्ष्ये मन्त्रं चतुर्वर्गसिद्ध्यै त्रैलिक्यमोहनम् /
ओं श्रीं ह्रीं ह्रूं ओं नमः पुरुशोत्तमः
पुरुषोत्तमप्रतिरूप लक्ष्मीनिवास सकलजगत्क्षोभण

स्तम्भय 2 द्रावय 2 आकर्षय 2 परमसुभग सर्वसौमाग्यकर

किन्तिष्ठसियावत्तावत् समीहितं मे सिद्धं भवति हूं फट्

306.m:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim the mantra that enchants the three worlds, for the attainment of the four goals of life.
Om śrīṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ. Om, obeisance to Puruṣottama, / the counter-image of Puruṣottama, abode of Lakṣmī, agitator of all the world, / cleaver of the hearts of all women, infatuator of the three worlds with passion, / torment, torment the minds of beautiful divine and mortal people; kindle, kindle; wither, wither; slay, slay; / paralyze, paralyze; liquefy, liquefy; attract, attract, O supremely fortunate one, bestower of all good fortune, / bestower of desires; strike, strike such-and-such a person with the discus, with the mace, with the sword, with all […]
[Page 127]
pierce, pierce with arrows; bind, bind with the noose; strike, strike with the elephant goad; quickly, quickly; / why do you wait until my desire is fulfilled? *Hūṃ phaṭ*, obeisance! / Om, O Puruṣottama, infatuator of the three worlds with passion, *hūṃ phaṭ*, obeisance to the heart; draw [them], O one of great might, *hūṃ phaṭ*, to the weapon; O Lord of the three worlds, / strike, strike the minds of all people, tear them open, tear them open, bring them under my control, bring them under my control, *hūṃ phaṭ*, / to the eye; O enchanter of the three worlds, O matchless Hṛṣīkeśa, / attractor of the hearts of all women, come, come, obeisance!

306.s: saṅgākṣiṇyāyakena nyāsaṃ mūlavadīritaṃ //
306.d: सङ्गाक्षिण्यायकेन न्यासं मूलवदीरितं //
306.m: The ritual deposition with the ancillary mantras is declared to be like the root mantra.

306.s:
iṣṭvā sañjapya pañcāśatsahasramabhiṣicya ca /
kuṇḍegnau devike vahnau kṛtvā śataṃ hunet //
306.d:
इष्ट्वा सञ्जप्य पञ्चाशत्सहस्रमभिषिच्य च /
कुण्डेग्नौ देविके वह्नौ कृत्वा शतं हुनेत् //
306.m: Having worshipped, recited fifty thousand times, and performed consecration by aspersion, / having made a fire in a pit for the deity, one should offer one hundred oblations in the fire:

306.s:
pṛthagdadhi ghṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ caruṃ sājyaṃ payaḥ śṛtaṃ /
dvādaśāhutimūlena sahasrañcākṣatāṃstilān //
306.d:
पृथग्दधि घृतं क्षीरं चरुं साज्यं पयः शृतं /
द्वादशाहुतिमूलेन सहस्रञ्चाक्षतांस्तिलान् //
306.m: separately curd, clarified butter, milk, sacrificial cooked food mixed with ghee, boiled milk, / with the root mantra for twelve oblations, and a thousand oblations of unhusked barley grains and sesamum,

306.s:
yavaṃ madhutrayaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ dadhi samicchataṃ /
hutvā pūrṇāhutiṃ śiṣṭaṃ prāśayetsaghṛtaṃ caruṃ //
306.d:
यवं मधुत्रयं पुष्पं फलं दधि समिच्छतं /
हुत्वा पूर्णाहुतिं शिष्टं प्राशयेत्सघृतं चरुं //
306.m: barley, the three sweets, flowers, fruits, and curd, as one desires. / Having offered the final oblation, one should consume the remaining sacrificial food with ghee.

306.s:
sambhojya viprānācāryaṃ toṣayetsidhyate manuḥ /
snātvā yathāvadācamya vāgyato yāgamandiraṃ //
306.d:
सम्भोज्य विप्रानाचार्यं तोषयेत्सिध्यते मनुः /
स्नात्वा यथावदाचम्य वाग्यतो यागमन्दिरं //
306.m: Having fed the Brahmins and gratified the preceptor, the mantra becomes efficacious. / Having bathed, sipped water according to the rules, and restrained speech, having gone to the sacrificial pavilion,

306.s:
gatvā padmāsanaṃ baddhvā śoṣayedvidhinā vapuḥ /
rakṣoghnavighnakṛddikṣu nyasedādau sudarśanam //
306.d:
गत्वा पद्मासनं बद्ध्वा शोषयेद्विधिना वपुः /
रक्षोघ्नविघ्नकृद्दिक्षु न्यसेदादौ सुदर्शनम् //
306.m: having assumed the lotus posture, one should purify the body according to rule. / First, one should ritually deposit Sudarśana in the cardinal directions to destroy demons and remove obstacles.

306.s:
pañcabījaṃ nābhimadhyasthaṃ dhūmraṃ caṇḍānilātmakam /
aśeṣaṃ kalmaṣaṃ dehāt viśleṣayadanusmaret //
306.d:
पञ्चबीजं नाभिमध्यस्थं धूम्रं चण्डानिलात्मकम् /
अशेषं कल्मषं देहात् विश्लेषयदनुस्मरेत् //
306.m: One should meditate on the seed syllable *yaṃ* situated in the center of the navel, smoky in color, consisting of fierce wind, / as separating all impurities from the body.

306.s:
raṃvījaṃ hṛdayābjasthaṃ smṛtvā jvālābhirādahet /
urdhvādhastiryagābhistu mūrdhni saṃplāvayedvapuḥ //
306.d:
रंवीजं हृदयाब्जस्थं स्मृत्वा ज्वालाभिरादहेत् /
उर्ध्वाधस्तिर्यगाभिस्तु मूर्ध्नि संप्लावयेद्वपुः //
306.m: Remembering the seed syllable *raṃ* situated in the lotus of the heart, one should burn [the body] with flames; / with these [flames] moving upward, downward, and horizontally, one should then flood the body at the crown of the head,

306.s:
dhyātvāmṛtair vahiścāntaḥsuṣumnāmārgagāmibhiḥ /
evaṃ śuddhavapuḥ prāṇānāyamya manunā tridhā //
:p 128
306.d:
ध्यात्वामृतैर् वहिश्चान्तःसुषुम्नामार्गगामिभिः /
एवं शुद्धवपुः प्राणानायम्य मनुना त्रिधा //
:प् 128
306.m:
meditating on nectars flowing outside and inside along the path of the suṣumnā. / The body thus purified, having controlled the vital breaths three times with the mantra,
[Page 128]

306.s:
vinyasennyastahastāntaḥ śaktiṃ mastakavaktrayoḥ /
guhye gale dikṣu hṛdi kakṣau dehe ca sarvataḥ //
306.d:
विन्यसेन्न्यस्तहस्तान्तः शक्तिं मस्तकवक्त्रयोः /
गुह्ये गले दिक्षु हृदि कक्षौ देहे च सर्वतः //
306.m: one should ritually deposit the power deposited in the hands onto the head, face, / private parts, throat, the directions, heart, armpits, and everywhere on the body.

306.s:
āvāhya brahmarandhreṇa hṛtpadme sūryamaṇḍalāt /
tāreṇa samparātmānaṃ smarettaṃ sarvalakṣaṇaṃ //
306.d:
आवाह्य ब्रह्मरन्ध्रेण हृत्पद्मे सूर्यमण्डलात् /
तारेण सम्परात्मानं स्मरेत्तं सर्वलक्षणं //
306.m: Having invoked [the Supreme Self] through the aperture of Brahmā into the heart-lotus from the solar orb / with the praṇava, one should meditate on that Supreme Self possessed of all auspicious marks:

306.s:
trailokyamohanāya vidmahe smarāya dhīmahi tanno viṣṇuḥ
pracodayāt
ātmārcanāt kratudravyaṃ prokṣayecchuddhapātrakaṃ /
/
kṛtvātmapūjāṃ vidhinā sthaṇḍile taṃ samarcayet //
306.d:
त्रैलोक्यमोहनाय विद्महे स्मराय धीमहि तन्नो विष्णुः
प्रचोदयात्
आत्मार्चनात् क्रतुद्रव्यं प्रोक्षयेच्छुद्धपात्रकं /
/
कृत्वात्मपूजां विधिना स्थण्डिले तं समर्चयेत् //
306.m: "We know the Enchanter of the Three Worlds; we meditate on the God of Love; may that Viṣṇu inspire us." / After self-worship, one should sprinkle the sacrificial substances and clean vessels; / having performed worship of oneself according to rule, one should worship him on an altar-mound,

306.s:
/
karmādikalpite pīṭhe padmasthaṃ garuḍopari /
/
marvāṅgasundaraṃ prāptavayolāvaṇyayauvanaṃ //
306.d:
/
कर्मादिकल्पिते पीठे पद्मस्थं गरुडोपरि /
/
मर्वाङ्गसुन्दरं प्राप्तवयोलावण्ययौवनं //
306.m: seated on a lotus upon Garuḍa on a throne constructed of rites and the rest, / handsome in all limbs, endowed with youthful charm and youthfulness,

306.s:
/
madāghūrṇitatāmrākṣamudāraṃ smaravihvaliṃ /
/
divyamālyāmvaralepabhūṣitaṃ sasmitānanaṃ //
306.d:
/
मदाघूर्णितताम्राक्षमुदारं स्मरविह्वलिं /
/
दिव्यमाल्याम्वरलेपभूषितं सस्मिताननं //
306.m: with red eyes rolling in intoxication, noble, languishing with love, / adorned with divine garlands, garments, and unguents, with a smiling face,

306.s:
/
viṣṇuṃ nānāvidhānekaparivāraparicchadam /
/
lokānugrahaṇaṃ saumyaṃ sahasrādityatejasaṃ //
306.d:
/
विष्णुं नानाविधानेकपरिवारपरिच्छदम् /
/
लोकानुग्रहणं सौम्यं सहस्रादित्यतेजसं //
306.m: Viṣṇu, attended by diverse and numerous attendants, / bestowing grace upon the worlds, gentle, possessing the radiance of a thousand suns,

306.s:
/
pañcavāṇadharaṃ prāptakāmaikṣaṃ dvicaturbhujam /
/
devastrībhirvṛtaṃ devīmukhāsaktekṣaṇaṃ japet //
306.d:
/
पञ्चवाणधरं प्राप्तकामैक्षं द्विचतुर्भुजम् /
/
देवस्त्रीभिर्वृतं देवीमुखासक्तेक्षणं जपेत् //
306.m: bearing five arrows, with eyes full of desire, having two or four arms, / surrounded by divine women, his gaze fixed on the face of the goddess—thus one should recite.

306.s:
/
cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ dhanuḥ khaḍgaṃ gadāṃmuṣalamaṅkuśaṃ /
/
pāśañca vibhrataṃ cārcedāvāhādivisargataḥ //
306.d:
/
चक्रं शङ्खं धनुः खड्गं गदांमुषलमङ्कुशं /
/
पाशञ्च विभ्रतं चार्चेदावाहादिविसर्गतः //
306.m: And one should worship [him] holding a discus, a conch, a bow, a sword, a mace, a pestle, a goad, / and a noose, from invocation through dismissal.

306.s:
/
śriyaṃ vāmorujaṅghāsthāṃ śliṣyantīṃ pāṇinā patiṃ /
/
sābjacāmarakarāṃ pīnāṃ śrīvatsakaustubhānvitāṃ //
306.d:
/
श्रियं वामोरुजङ्घास्थां श्लिष्यन्तीं पाणिना पतिं /
/
साब्जचामरकरां पीनां श्रीवत्सकौस्तुभान्वितां //
306.m: [And one should worship] Śrī situated on his left thigh and shank, embracing her lord with her hand, / with a lotus and chowrie in her hands, plump, endowed with the Śrīvatsa and Kaustubha,

306.s:
/
mālinaṃ pītavastrañca cakrādyāḍhyaṃ hariṃ yajet /
/
oṃ sudarśana mahācakrarāja duṣṭabhayaṅkara chida 2 chinda 2
vidāraya 2 paramamantrān grasa 2 bhakṣaya 2 bhūtāni cāśapa 2
hūṃ
:p 129
phaṭ oṃ jalacarāya svāhā / khaḍgatīkṣṇa chinda 2 khaḍgāya
namaḥ / śāraṅgāya saśarāya hūṃ phaṭ / bhūtagrāmāya
vidmahe caturvidhāya dhīmahi tanno brahma pracodayāt / sambartaka śvasana
pothaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ svāhā / pāśa bandha 2 ākarṣaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ
/ aṅkuśena kaṭṭa hūṃ phaṭ
kramādbhujeṣu mantraiḥ svair ebhirastrāṇi pūjayet //
oṃ pakṣirājāya hrūṃ phaṭ
306.d:
/
मालिनं पीतवस्त्रञ्च चक्राद्याढ्यं हरिं यजेत् /
/
ओं सुदर्शन महाचक्रराज दुष्टभयङ्कर छिद 2 छिन्द 2
विदारय 2 परममन्त्रान् ग्रस 2 भक्षय 2 भूतानि चाशप 2
हूं
:प् 129
फट् ओं जलचराय स्वाहा / खड्गतीक्ष्ण छिन्द 2 खड्गाय
नमः / शारङ्गाय सशराय हूं फट् / भूतग्रामाय
विद्महे चतुर्विधाय धीमहि तन्नो ब्रह्म प्रचोदयात् / सम्बर्तक श्वसन
पोथय 2 हूं फट् स्वाहा / पाश बन्ध 2 आकर्षय 2 हूं फट्
/ अङ्कुशेन कट्ट हूं फट्
क्रमाद्भुजेषु मन्त्रैः स्वैर् एभिरस्त्राणि पूजयेत् //
ओं पक्षिराजाय ह्रूं फट्
306.m:
wearing a garland and yellow garments, rich in discus and other [weapons]: one should worship Hari:
“Oṃ, O Sudarśana, king of great discuses, terrifier of the wicked! Cut, cut! Cleave, cleave! / Tear apart, tear apart! Devour, devour other mantras! Consume, consume! Curse, curse the spirits! Hūṃ
phaṭ! Oṃ, svāhā to the aquatic creature! Sharp as a sword, cleave, cleave! Homage to the sword!
To the Śāraṅga [bow] with arrow, hūṃ phaṭ! We know the aggregate of elements; we contemplate the fourfold; may that Brahman impel us! Destroyer, breath of wind, / crush, crush, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā! O noose, bind, bind! Attract, attract, hūṃ phaṭ! / Strike with the goad, hūṃ phaṭ!” / In due order upon the arms, one should worship the weapons with their respective mantras.
“Oṃ, to the king of birds, hrūṃ phaṭ!”

306.s:
tārkṣyaṃ yajet karṇikāyāmaṅgadevān yathāvidhi /
śāktirindrādiyantreṣu tārkṣyādyā dhṛtacāmarāḥ //
306.d:
तार्क्ष्यं यजेत् कर्णिकायामङ्गदेवान् यथाविधि /
शाक्तिरिन्द्रादियन्त्रेषु तार्क्ष्याद्या धृतचामराः //
306.m: One should worship Tārkṣya on the pericarp, [and] the limb deities according to rule; / the Śakti on the diagrams of Indra and others; Tārkṣya and others holding chowries.

306.s:
śaktayo 'nte prayojyādau sureśādyāś ca daṇḍinā /
pīte lakṣmīsarasvatyau ratiprītijayāḥ sitāḥ //
306.d:
शक्तयो ऽन्ते प्रयोज्यादौ सुरेशाद्याश् च दण्डिना /
पीते लक्ष्मीसरस्वत्यौ रतिप्रीतिजयाः सिताः //
306.m: The Śaktis are to be employed at the end; in the beginning, the lords of the gods and others, along with Daṇḍin. / On the yellow, Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī; Rati, Prīti, and Jayā are white;

306.s:
kīrtikāntyau site śyāme tuṣṭipuṣṭyau smarodite /
lokeśāntaṃ yajeddevaṃ viṣṇumiṣṭārthasiddhaye //
306.d:
कीर्तिकान्त्यौ सिते श्यामे तुष्टिपुष्ट्यौ स्मरोदिते /
लोकेशान्तं यजेद्देवं विष्णुमिष्टार्थसिद्धये //
306.m: Kīrti and Kānti are white and dark; Tuṣṭi and Puṣṭi are uttered by Smara. / One should worship the god Viṣṇu up to the world-protectors for the accomplishment of desired aims.

306.s:
dhyāyenmantraṃ japitvainaṃ juhuyāttvabhiśecayet /
oṃ śrīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ trailokyamohanāya viṣṇave
namaḥ
etatpūjādinā sarvān kāmānāpnoti pūrvavat //
306.d:
ध्यायेन्मन्त्रं जपित्वैनं जुहुयात्त्वभिशेचयेत् /
ओं श्रीं क्रीं ह्रीं हूं त्रैलोक्यमोहनाय विष्णवे
नमः
एतत्पूजादिना सर्वान् कामानाप्नोति पूर्ववत् //
306.m:
Having meditated and recited this mantra, one should offer fire oblations and perform aspersion:
“Oṃ śrīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, homage to Viṣṇu, the bewitcher of the three worlds!”
By means of worship and the like with this [mantra], one obtains all desires as before.

306.s:
toyaiḥ sammohanī puṣpair nityantena ca tarpayet /
brahmā saśakraśrīdaṇḍī vījaṃ trailokyamohanam //
306.d:
तोयैः सम्मोहनी पुष्पैर् नित्यन्तेन च तर्पयेत् /
ब्रह्मा सशक्रश्रीदण्डी वीजं त्रैलोक्यमोहनम् //
306.m: One should continually gratify her with water and enchanting flowers; / Brahmā with Śakra, Śrī, and Daṇḍī is the seed syllable [which is] the bewitcher of the three worlds.

306.s:
japtvā trilakṣaṃ hutvā ca lakṣaṃ bilvaiś ca sājyakaiḥ /
taṇḍulaiḥ phalagandhādyaiḥ(1) dūrvābhistvāyurāpnuyāt //
306.d:
जप्त्वा त्रिलक्षं हुत्वा च लक्षं बिल्वैश् च साज्यकैः /
तण्डुलैः फलगन्धाद्यैः(1) दूर्वाभिस्त्वायुराप्नुयात् //
306.m: Having recited three hundred thousand times and offered fire oblations a hundred thousand times with bilva leaves and ghee, / with unhusked rice, fruits, perfumes, and other [offerings], and with dūrvā grass, one obtains long life.

306.s:
tayābhiṣekahomādikriyātuṣṭo hy abhīṣṭadaḥ /
:n
1 phalapuṣpādyair iti ṭa..
:p 130
oṃ namo bhagavate varāhāya bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥpataye bhūpatidvaṃ me
dehi hṛdayāya svāha
pañcāṅgaṃ nityamayutaṃ japtvāyūrājyamāpnuyāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe trailokyamohanamantro nāma
ṣaṣṭhādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
trailokyamohanīlakṣmyādipūjā
306.d:
तयाभिषेकहोमादिक्रियातुष्टो ह्य् अभीष्टदः /
:न्
1 फलपुष्पाद्यैर् इति ट..
:प् 130
ओं नमो भगवते वराहाय भूर्भुवः स्वःपतये भूपतिद्वं मे
देहि हृदयाय स्वाह
पञ्चाङ्गं नित्यमयुतं जप्त्वायूराज्यमाप्नुयात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे त्रैलोक्यमोहनमन्त्रो नाम
षष्ठाधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्ताधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
त्रैलोक्यमोहनीलक्ष्म्यादिपूजा
306.m:
Pleased indeed by the rites of aspersion, fire oblation, and the rest with that [mantra], he grants one's desired wishes.
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript ṭa: "phalapuṣpādyaiḥ".
[Page 130]
“Oṃ namo bhagavate Varāhāya, lord of the earth, atmosphere, and heaven! Grant me lordship of the earth! Svāhā to the heart!” / Reciting [this] five-limbed [mantra] ten thousand times daily, one obtains long life and kingship.
Thus ends the three hundred and sixth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, called the Trailokyamohana Mantra.
Now, the three hundred and seventh chapter.
Worship of Trailokyamohanī Lakṣmī and others.

307.s:
agnir uvāca
vakṣaḥ savahniryāmākṣau daṇḍīḥ śrīḥ sarvasiddhidā /
mahāśriye mahāsiddhe mahāvidyutprabhe namaḥ //
śriye devi vijaye namaḥ / gauri mahābale bandha 2 namaḥ / hūṃ
mahākāye padmahaste hūṃ phaṭ śriyai namaḥ / śriyai phaṭ śriyai
namaḥ / śriyai phaṭ śrīṃ namaḥ / śriye śrīda namaḥ
svāhā svāhā śrīphaṭ ||
307.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वक्षः सवह्निर्यामाक्षौ दण्डीः श्रीः सर्वसिद्धिदा /
महाश्रिये महासिद्धे महाविद्युत्प्रभे नमः //
श्रिये देवि विजये नमः / गौरि महाबले बन्ध 2 नमः / हूं
महाकाये पद्महस्ते हूं फट् श्रियै नमः / श्रियै फट् श्रियै
नमः / श्रियै फट् श्रीं नमः / श्रिये श्रीद नमः
स्वाहा स्वाहा श्रीफट् ||
307.m:
Agni said: / The chest with fire, the southern eye, Daṇḍīḥ, Śrīḥ, the grantor of all success: / “Homage to Mahāśrī, possessing great attainments, shining like great lightning!
Homage to Śrī, O Goddess Vijayā! O Gaurī, possessing great strength, bind, bind, homage! Hūṃ, / O you of great body, lotus in hand, hūṃ phaṭ homage to Śrī! To Śrī phaṭ, to Śrī / homage! To Śrī phaṭ, śrīṃ homage! To Śrī, O bestower of prosperity, homage, / svāhā svāhā, śrī phaṭ!”

307.s:
asyāṅgāni navoktāni teṣvekañca samāśrayet /
trilakṣamekalakṣaṃ vā japtvākṣābjaiś ca bhūtidaḥ //
307.d:
अस्याङ्गानि नवोक्तानि तेष्वेकञ्च समाश्रयेत् /
त्रिलक्षमेकलक्षं वा जप्त्वाक्षाब्जैश् च भूतिदः //
307.m: Her nine limbs have been stated; one should resort to one among them. / Having recited three hundred thousand or one hundred thousand times with rosaries of lotus seeds, one becomes a bestower of prosperity.

307.s:
śrīgehe viṣṇugehe vā śriyaṃ pūjya dhanaṃ labhet /
ājyāktaistaṇḍulair lakṣaṃ juhuyāt khādirānale //
307.d:
श्रीगेहे विष्णुगेहे वा श्रियं पूज्य धनं लभेत् /
आज्याक्तैस्तण्डुलैर् लक्षं जुहुयात् खादिरानले //
307.m: Having worshipped Śrī in a temple of Śrī or in a temple of Viṣṇu, one obtains wealth. / One should offer a hundred thousand oblations of grains of rice smeared with ghee into a fire of khadira wood.

307.s:
rājā vaśyo bhavedvṛddhiḥ śrīś ca syāduttarottaraṃ /
sarṣapāmbhobhiṣekeṇa naśyante sakalā grahāḥ //
307.d:
राजा वश्यो भवेद्वृद्धिः श्रीश् च स्यादुत्तरोत्तरं /
सर्षपाम्भोभिषेकेण नश्यन्ते सकला ग्रहाः //
307.m: A king becomes subjugated, prosperity increases, and Śrī increases more and more. / By aspersion with mustard water, all planetary afflictions are destroyed.

307.s:
bilvalakṣahutā lakṣmīrvittavṛddhiś ca jāyate /
śakraveśma caturdvāraṃ hṛdaye cintayedatha //
:p 131
307.d:
बिल्वलक्षहुता लक्ष्मीर्वित्तवृद्धिश् च जायते /
शक्रवेश्म चतुर्द्वारं हृदये चिन्तयेदथ //
:प् 131
307.m:
Lakṣmī and increase of wealth arise from a hundred thousand oblations with bilva. / Then one should contemplate in the heart the four-doored abode of Indra.
[Page 131]

307.s:
balākāṃ vāmanāṃ śyāmāṃ śvetapaṅkajadhāriṇīm /
ūrdhvavāhudvayaṃ dhyāyetkrīḍantīṃ dvāri pūrvavat //
307.d:
बलाकां वामनां श्यामां श्वेतपङ्कजधारिणीम् /
ऊर्ध्ववाहुद्वयं ध्यायेत्क्रीडन्तीं द्वारि पूर्ववत् //
307.m: One should meditate on Balākā at the door as before, short, dark, holding a white lotus, / with her two arms raised, sporting.

307.s:
urdhvīkṛtena hastena raktapaṅkajadhāriṇīṃ /
śvetāṅgīṃ dakṣiṇe dvāri cintayedvanamālinīm //
307.d:
उर्ध्वीकृतेन हस्तेन रक्तपङ्कजधारिणीं /
श्वेताङ्गीं दक्षिणे द्वारि चिन्तयेद्वनमालिनीम् //
307.m: At the southern door one should contemplate [the deity] holding a red lotus with a raised hand, / having a white body, wearing a garland of forest flowers.

307.s:
haritāṃ dordvayenordhamudvahantīṃ sitāmbujam /
dhyāyedvibhīṣikāṃ nāma śrīdūtīṃ dvāri paścime //
307.d:
हरितां दोर्द्वयेनोर्धमुद्वहन्तीं सिताम्बुजम् /
ध्यायेद्विभीषिकां नाम श्रीदूतीं द्वारि पश्चिमे //
307.m: At the western door one should meditate on Vibhīṣikā by name, the messenger of Śrī, / green, lifting up a white lotus with her two arms.

307.s:
śāṅkarīmukktare dvāri tanmadhye 'ṣṭadalapaṅkajaṃ /
vāsudevaḥ saṅkarṣaṇaḥ pradyumnaścāniruddhakaḥ //
307.d:
शाङ्करीमुक्क्तरे द्वारि तन्मध्ये ऽष्टदलपङ्कजं /
वासुदेवः सङ्कर्षणः प्रद्युम्नश्चानिरुद्धकः //
307.m: [One should meditate on] Śāṅkarī at the northern door; in the middle of it is an eight-petaled lotus: / Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha.

307.s:
dhyeyāste padmapatreṣu śaṅkhacakragadādharāḥ /
añjanakṣīrakāśmīrahemābhāste suvāsasaḥ //
307.d:
ध्येयास्ते पद्मपत्रेषु शङ्खचक्रगदाधराः /
अञ्जनक्षीरकाश्मीरहेमाभास्ते सुवाससः //
307.m: They are to be meditated upon on the lotus petals, holding a conch, discus, and mace, / resembling collyrium, milk, saffron, and gold, wearing handsome garments.

307.s:
āgneyādiṣu patreṣu gugguluś ca kuruṇṭakaḥ /
damakaḥ salilaśceti hastinī rajataprabhāḥ //
307.d:
आग्नेयादिषु पत्रेषु गुग्गुलुश् च कुरुण्टकः /
दमकः सलिलश्चेति हस्तिनी रजतप्रभाः //
307.m: On the petals beginning with the southeast: Guggulu, Kuruṇṭaka, / Damaka, Salila, and Hastinī, radiant like silver.

307.s:
hemakumbhadharāś caite karṇikāyāṃ śriyaṃ smaret /
caturbhujāṃ suvarṇābhāṃ sapadmordhvabhujadvayāṃ //
307.d:
हेमकुम्भधराश् चैते कर्णिकायां श्रियं स्मरेत् /
चतुर्भुजां सुवर्णाभां सपद्मोर्ध्वभुजद्वयां //
307.m: These hold golden pots; and on the pericarp one should remember Śrī: / four-armed, golden-hued, having two upper arms with lotuses,

307.s:
dakṣiṇābhayahastābhāṃ vāmahastavarapradāṃ /
śvetagandhāṃśukāmekaraumyamālāstradhāriṇīṃ //
307.d:
दक्षिणाभयहस्ताभां वामहस्तवरप्रदां /
श्वेतगन्धांशुकामेकरौम्यमालास्त्रधारिणीं //
307.m: with her right hand bestowing fearlessness and her left hand granting boons, / wearing white fragrant garments, holding a single silver garland and weapons.

307.s:
dhyātvā saparivārāntāmabhyarcya sakalaṃ labhet /
droṇābjapuṣpaśrīvṛkṣaparṇaṃ mūrdhni na dhārayet //
307.d:
ध्यात्वा सपरिवारान्तामभ्यर्च्य सकलं लभेत् /
द्रोणाब्जपुष्पश्रीवृक्षपर्णं मूर्ध्नि न धारयेत् //
307.m: Having meditated on her along with her retinue and worshipped her, one obtains everything. / One should not place a droṇa leaf, a lotus flower, or a bilva leaf on one's head.

307.s:
lavaṇāmalakaṃ varjyaṃ nāgādityatithau kramāt /
pāyasāśī japet sūktaṃ śriyastenābhiṣecayet //
307.d:
लवणामलकं वर्ज्यं नागादित्यतिथौ क्रमात् /
पायसाशी जपेत् सूक्तं श्रियस्तेनाभिषेचयेत् //
307.m: Salt and myrobalan are to be avoided on the fifth and seventh lunar days, respectively. / Subsisting on milk-rice, one should recite the hymn of Śrī and perform aspersion with it.

307.s:
āvāhādivisargāntāṃ mūrdhni dhyātvārcayet śriyam /
vilvājyābjapāyasena pṛthak yogaḥ śriye bhavet //
307.d:
आवाहादिविसर्गान्तां मूर्ध्नि ध्यात्वार्चयेत् श्रियम् /
विल्वाज्याब्जपायसेन पृथक् योगः श्रिये भवेत् //
307.m: Having meditated on Śrī upon one's head, one should worship her from invocation through dismissal. / With bilva, ghee, lotuses, and milk-rice, there is an individual rite for [attaining] Śrī.

307.s:
viṣaṃ mahiṣakāntāgnirudrijyotirvakadvayam /
:p 132
oṃ hrīṃ mahāmahiṣamardini ṭha ṭha mūlamantraṃ
bhahiṣahiṃsake namaḥ / mahiṣaśatruṃ bhrāmaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ
ṭha ṭha mahiṣaṃ heṣaya 2 hūṃ mahiṣaṃ hana2 devi hūṃ
mahiṣanisūdani phaṭ
durgāhṛdayamityuktaṃ sāṅgaṃ sarvārthasādhakam //
307.d:
विषं महिषकान्ताग्निरुद्रिज्योतिर्वकद्वयम् /
:प् 132
ओं ह्रीं महामहिषमर्दिनि ठ ठ मूलमन्त्रं
भहिषहिंसके नमः / महिषशत्रुं भ्रामय 2 हूं फट्
ठ ठ महिषं हेषय 2 हूं महिषं हन2 देवि हूं
महिषनिसूदनि फट्
दुर्गाहृदयमित्युक्तं साङ्गं सर्वार्थसाधकम् //
307.m:
Poison, the beloved of Mahiṣa, fire, Rudra, light, a pair of cranes—
[Page 132]
“Oṃ hrīṃ, O great crusher of Mahiṣa, ṭha ṭha!” is the root mantra. / “Homage to the slayer of Mahiṣa! Whirl, whirl the enemy Mahiṣa, hūṃ phaṭ / ṭha ṭha! Make Mahiṣa neigh, neigh, hūṃ! Slay, slay Mahiṣa, O Goddess, hūṃ / O slayer of Mahiṣa, phaṭ!” / This is declared to be the Durgā-hṛdaya along with its limbs, which accomplishes all ends.

307.s:
/
yajedyathoktaṃ tāṃ devīṃ pīṭhañcaivāṅgamadhyagam /
/
oṃ hrīṃ durge rakṣaṇi svāhā ceti durgāyai namaḥ / varavarṇyai
namaḥ / āryāyai kanakaprabhāyai kṛttikāyai abhayapradāyai kanyakāyai
surūpāyai ||
patrasthāḥ pūjayedetā mūrtīrādyaiḥ svaraiḥ kramāt //
307.d:
/
यजेद्यथोक्तं तां देवीं पीठञ्चैवाङ्गमध्यगम् /
/
ओं ह्रीं दुर्गे रक्षणि स्वाहा चेति दुर्गायै नमः / वरवर्ण्यै
नमः / आर्यायै कनकप्रभायै कृत्तिकायै अभयप्रदायै कन्यकायै
सुरूपायै ||
पत्रस्थाः पूजयेदेता मूर्तीराद्यैः स्वरैः क्रमात् //
307.m:
One should worship that Goddess as prescribed, and the pedestal situated in the midst of the limbs.
“Oṃ hrīṃ, O Durgā, O protectress, svāhā”; and “Homage to Durgā, / homage to the fair-complexioned one, / to Āryā, to the golden-hued one, to Kṛttikā, to the grantor of fearlessness, to the maiden, / to the shapely one.”
One should worship these icons situated on the petals in order, with the initial vowels.

307.s:
cakrāya śaṅkhāya gadāyai khaḍgāya dhanuṣe vāṇāya /
aṣṭamyādyair imāṃ durgāṃ lokeśāntāṃ yajediti /
durgāyogaḥ samāyuḥśrīsvāmiraktājayādikṛt //
307.d:
चक्राय शङ्खाय गदायै खड्गाय धनुषे वाणाय /
अष्टम्याद्यैर् इमां दुर्गां लोकेशान्तां यजेदिति /
दुर्गायोगः समायुःश्रीस्वामिरक्ताजयादिकृत् //
307.m: To the discus, to the conch, to the mace, to the sword, to the bow, to the arrow. / With [rites on] the eighth [lunar day] and others, one should thus worship this Durgā ending with the world-protectors. / The Durgā ritual produces a full lifespan, prosperity, devotion of the master, victory, and the like.

307.s:
samādhyeśānamantreṇa tilahomo vaśīkaraḥ /
jayaḥ padmaistu durvābhiḥ śāntiḥ kāmaḥ palāśajaiḥ //
307.d:
समाध्येशानमन्त्रेण तिलहोमो वशीकरः /
जयः पद्मैस्तु दुर्वाभिः शान्तिः कामः पलाशजैः //
307.m: Fire oblation of sesame seeds with the Īśāna mantra in meditation produces subjugation; / with lotuses, victory; with dūrvā grass, pacification; with palāśa blossoms, desire;

307.s:
puṣṭiḥ syāt kākapakṣeṇa mṛtidveṣādikaṃ bhavet /
brahmakṣudrabhayāpattiṃ sarvameva manurharet //
oṃ durge durge rakṣaṇi svāhā
307.d:
पुष्टिः स्यात् काकपक्षेण मृतिद्वेषादिकं भवेत् /
ब्रह्मक्षुद्रभयापत्तिं सर्वमेव मनुर्हरेत् //
ओं दुर्गे दुर्गे रक्षणि स्वाहा
307.m:
with crow feathers, there will be nourishment, death, enmity, and the like. / This mantra removes all danger and misfortune arising from Brahmins and petty spirits.
“Oṃ, O Durgā, Durgā, O protectress, svāhā!”

307.s:
rakṣākarīyamuditā jayadurgāṅgasaṃyutā /
śyāmāṃ trilicanāṃ devīṃ dhyātvātmānaṃ caturbhujam //
307.d:
रक्षाकरीयमुदिता जयदुर्गाङ्गसंयुता /
श्यामां त्रिलिचनां देवीं ध्यात्वात्मानं चतुर्भुजम् //
307.m: This is declared to be the protective [goddess], accompanied by the limbs of Jayadurgā. / Having meditated on the dark, three-eyed Goddess, and on oneself as four-armed,

307.s:
śaṅkhacakrābjaśūlāditriśūlāṃ raudrarūpiṇīṃ /
yuddhādau sañjayedetāṃ yajet khaḍgādike jaye //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe trailokyamohanīlakṣmyādipūjā nāma
saptādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 133
:ś athāṣṭādhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
tvaritāpūjā
307.d:
शङ्खचक्राब्जशूलादित्रिशूलां रौद्ररूपिणीं /
युद्धादौ सञ्जयेदेतां यजेत् खड्गादिके जये //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे त्रैलोक्यमोहनीलक्ष्म्यादिपूजा नाम
सप्ताधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 133
:श् अथाष्टाधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
त्वरितापूजा
307.m:
Bearing a conch, discus, lotus, trident, and other weapons, of fierce form, / one should invoke her in battle and similar occasions, and worship her for victory by means of swords and the like.
Thus ends the three hundred and seventh chapter, entitled "Worship of Trailokyamohanī, Lakṣmī, and Others," in the Agni Mahāpurāṇa.
Now, the three hundred and eighth chapter.
Worship of Tvaritā.

308.s:
agnir uvāca
tvaritāṅgānsamākhyāsye bhuktimuktipradāyakān /
oṃ ādhāraśaktyai namaḥ / oṃ hrīṃ puru 2 mahāsiṃhāya
namaḥ /oṃ padmāya namaḥ / oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ khecachekṣaḥ /
strīṃ oṃ hrūṃ kṣaiṃ hrūṃ phaṭ tvaritāyai namaḥ / khe ca
hṛdayāya namaḥ /cache śirase namaḥ /chekṣaḥ śikhāyai
namaḥ / kṣastrī kavacāya namaḥ / strīṃ hrūṃ netrāya namaḥ
/ hrūṃ khe astrāya phaṭ namaḥ / oṃ tvaritāvidyāṃ vidmahe
tūrṇavidyāñca dhīmahi tanno devī pracodayāt / śrīpraṇitāyai
namaḥ / hrūṃ kārāyai namaḥ / oṃ kheca hṛdayāya namaḥ /
khecaryai namaḥ / oṃ caṇḍāyai namaḥ / chedanyai namaḥ
kṣepaṇyai namaḥ /striyai hrūṃ kāryai namaḥ / kṣemaṅkaryai
jayāyai kiṅkarāya rakṣa / oṃ tvaritājñayā sthiro bhava vaṣaṭ
totalā tvaritā tūrṇetyetyevaṃ vidyeyamīritā //
308.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
त्वरिताङ्गान्समाख्यास्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकान् /
ओं आधारशक्त्यै नमः / ओं ह्रीं पुरु 2 महासिंहाय
नमः /ओं पद्माय नमः / ओं ह्रीं ह्रूं खेचछेक्षः /
स्त्रीं ओं ह्रूं क्षैं ह्रूं फट् त्वरितायै नमः / खे च
हृदयाय नमः /चछे शिरसे नमः /छेक्षः शिखायै
नमः / क्षस्त्री कवचाय नमः / स्त्रीं ह्रूं नेत्राय नमः
/ ह्रूं खे अस्त्राय फट् नमः / ओं त्वरिताविद्यां विद्महे
तूर्णविद्याञ्च धीमहि तन्नो देवी प्रचोदयात् / श्रीप्रणितायै
नमः / ह्रूं कारायै नमः / ओं खेच हृदयाय नमः /
खेचर्यै नमः / ओं चण्डायै नमः / छेदन्यै नमः
क्षेपण्यै नमः /स्त्रियै ह्रूं कार्यै नमः / क्षेमङ्कर्यै
जयायै किङ्कराय रक्ष / ओं त्वरिताज्ञया स्थिरो भव वषट्
तोतला त्वरिता तूर्णेत्येत्येवं विद्येयमीरिता //
308.m:
Agni said: / I shall now fully declare the limb-mantras of Tvaritā, which bestow worldly enjoyment and liberation:
"Oṃ, homage to the Support Śakti! Oṃ hrīṃ puru puru, homage to the Great Lion!
Homage! Oṃ, homage to the lotus! Oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ khecachekṣaḥ!
Strīṃ oṃ hrūṃ kṣaiṃ hrūṃ phaṭ, homage to Tvaritā! Khe ca, homage to the heart! Cache, homage to the head! Chekṣaḥ, homage to the topknot! Kṣastrī, homage to the armor! Strīṃ hrūṃ, homage to the eyes! Hrūṃ khe, phaṭ, homage to the weapon! Oṃ, we know the Tvaritā knowledge; we meditate on the swift knowledge; may the goddess impel us thereto! Homage to Śrīpraṇītā!
Homage to Hrūṅkārā! Oṃ kheca, homage to the heart!
Homage to Khecarī! Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍā! Homage to Chedanī! Homage to Kṣepaṇī! Striyai, homage to Hrūṅkārī! To Kṣemaṅkarī, to Jayā, to Kiṅkara, protect! Oṃ, by the command of Tvaritā, become steadfast, vaṣaṭ!"
Totalā, Tvaritā, Tūrṇā—thus has this mantra been proclaimed.

308.s:
śirobhrumastake kaṇṭhe hṛdi nābhau ca guhyake /
urvoś ca jānujaṅghorudvaye caraṇayoḥ kramāt //
308.d:
शिरोभ्रुमस्तके कण्ठे हृदि नाभौ च गुह्यके /
उर्वोश् च जानुजङ्घोरुद्वये चरणयोः क्रमात् //
308.m: Upon the head, between the brows, the crown of the head, the throat, the heart, the navel, and the privities, / on both thighs, the knees, the two shanks, and both feet in order:

308.s:
nyastāṅgo nyastamantrastu samastaṃ vyāpakaṃ nyaset /
pārvatī śavarī ceśā varadābhayahastikā //
308.d:
न्यस्ताङ्गो न्यस्तमन्त्रस्तु समस्तं व्यापकं न्यसेत् /
पार्वती शवरी चेशा वरदाभयहस्तिका //
308.m: having performed the ritual deposition of the limbs and the mantra, one should perform the pervasive ritual deposition over the whole [body]. / She is Pārvatī, a Śabarī tribal woman and the supreme sovereign, her hands granting boons and protection,
wearing bracelets of peacock [feathers], her diadem of peacock feathers, her garments of tender shoots, / seated upon a lion throne, accompanied by a parasol of peacock feathers,

308.s:
trinetrā śyāmalā devī vanamālāvibhūṣaṇā /
:p 134
viprāhikaṇrābharaṇā catrakeyūrabhūṣaṇā //
308.d:
त्रिनेत्रा श्यामला देवी वनमालाविभूषणा /
:प् 134
विप्राहिकण्राभरणा चत्रकेयूरभूषणा //
308.m:
three-eyed, dark-complexioned goddess, adorned with a garland of wild flowers,
[Page 134]
wearing a brahmin serpent as her ear ornament, decorated with armlets [of serpents],

308.s:
vaiśyanāgakaṭībandhā vṛṣalāhikṛtanūpurā /
evaṃ rūpātmikā bhūtvā tanmantraṃ niyutaṃ japet //
308.d:
वैश्यनागकटीबन्धा वृषलाहिकृतनूपुरा /
एवं रूपात्मिका भूत्वा तन्मन्त्रं नियुतं जपेत् //
308.m: with a vaiśya serpent as her girdle, and an outcast serpent made into her anklets. / Having become of such a form, one should recite her mantra one hundred thousand times.

308.s:
īśaḥ kirātarūpo 'bhūt purā gaurī ca tādṛśī /
