then on the western [petal]: ‘Oṃ dhṛ dhṛ nānā vāṃ vāṃ, O deathless one, / O origin of death, Śiva, supreme self of all, Mahādeva, lord of real existence, of great splendor,
lord of yoga, release, release! crush, crush! oṃ sarva 2, oṃ bhava 2, oṃ origin of Bhava!
Bestower of happiness on all beings!’ On the Vāyu petal, then in niyati, and in puruṣa, and on the northern petal:
‘Presence of all, higher than Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra, unworshipped, unpraised, witness 2, / turu 2, bird, Piṅga 2, knowledge 2, sound 2, subtle 2, Śiva 2, bestower of all 2, / oṃ, homage to Śiva, oṃ homage, homage to Śiva, oṃ homage, homage!’
In the northeast, in the prākṛta-tattva, one should worship, offer oblations, and recite.
This pacifies the distress caused by planets, diseases, and māyā, and yields all perfections.
Thus ends the three hundred and twenty-third chapter, entitled “Pacification by Rudra,” in the great Āgneya Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and twenty-fourth chapter:
The Divisions and Related Topics

324.s:
īśvara uvāca
rudrākṣakaṭakaṃ dhāryaṃ viṣamaṃ susamaṃ dṛḍam /
ekatripañcavadanaṃ yathālābhantu dhārayet //
324.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
रुद्राक्षकटकं धार्यं विषमं सुसमं दृडम् /
एकत्रिपञ्चवदनं यथालाभन्तु धारयेत् //
324.m: The Lord said: / A bracelet of rudrākṣa beads, odd or even, firm, should be worn; / one should wear a one-, three-, or five-faced bead as available.

324.s:
dvicatuḥṣaṇmukhaṃ śastamavraṇaṃ tīvrakaṇṭhakaṃ /
dakṣavāhau śikhādau ca dhārayeccaturānanaṃ //
324.d:
द्विचतुःषण्मुखं शस्तमव्रणं तीव्रकण्ठकं /
दक्षवाहौ शिखादौ च धारयेच्चतुराननं //
324.m: Two-, four-, and six-faced beads are recommended, unblemished and with sharp thorns; / one should wear a four-faced one on the right arm and at the topknot and so forth.

324.s:
abrahmacārī brahmacārī asnātaḥ snātako bhavet /
haimī vā mudrikā dhāryā(1) śivamantreṇa cārcya tu //
:n
1 kāryeti kha..
:p 177
324.d:
अब्रह्मचारी ब्रह्मचारी अस्नातः स्नातको भवेत् /
हैमी वा मुद्रिका धार्या(1) शिवमन्त्रेण चार्च्य तु //
:न्
1 कार्येति ख..
:प् 177
324.m:
A non-celibate becomes a celibate, an unbathed person becomes a cleansed bather; / or a golden ring should be worn, having worshipped [it] with the Śiva-mantra.
[Footnote]
1. "kāryā" in manuscript kha.. / :p 177

324.s:
śivaḥ śikhā tathā jyotiḥ savitraścetigocarāḥ /
gocarantu kulaṃ jñeyaṃ tena lakṣyastu dīkṣitaḥ //
324.d:
शिवः शिखा तथा ज्योतिः सवित्रश्चेतिगोचराः /
गोचरन्तु कुलं ज्ञेयं तेन लक्ष्यस्तु दीक्षितः //
324.m: The gocaras are Śiva, Śikhā, Jyotis, and Sāvitra; / and a gocara is to be known as a lineage, by which an initiate is characterized.

324.s:
prājāpatyo mahīpālaḥ kapoto granthikaḥ śive /
kuṭilāś caiva vetālāḥ padmahaṃsāḥ śikhākule //
324.d:
प्राजापत्यो महीपालः कपोतो ग्रन्थिकः शिवे /
कुटिलाश् चैव वेतालाः पद्महंसाः शिखाकुले //
324.m: Prājāpatya, Mahīpāla, Kapota, and Granthika are under Śiva; / Kuṭilas, Vetālas, Padmas, and Haṃsas are in the Śikhā lineage;

324.s:
dhṛtarāṣṭrā vakāḥ kākā gopālā jyotisaṃjñake /
kuṭikā sāṭharāś caiva guṭikā daṇḍino 'pare //
324.d:
धृतराष्ट्रा वकाः काका गोपाला ज्योतिसंज्ञके /
कुटिका साठराश् चैव गुटिका दण्डिनो ऽपरे //
324.m: Dhṛtarāṣṭras, cranes, crows, and cowherds are in the one named Jyotis; / Kuṭikas, Sāṭharas, Guṭikas, and staff-bearers are the others

324.s:
sāvitrī gocare caivamekaikastu caturvidhaḥ /
siddhādyaṃśakamākhyāsye yena mantraḥsusiddhidaḥ //
324.d:
सावित्री गोचरे चैवमेकैकस्तु चतुर्विधः /
सिद्धाद्यंशकमाख्यास्ये येन मन्त्रःसुसिद्धिदः //
324.m: in the gocara of Sāvitrī; thus each is of four kinds. / I shall explain the divisions such as siddha, by which a mantra gives complete success.

324.s:
bhūmau tu mātṛkā lekhyāḥ kūṭaṣaṇḍāvavarjitāḥ /
mantrākṣarāṇi viśliṣya anusvāraṃ nayet pṛthak //
324.d:
भूमौ तु मातृका लेख्याः कूटषण्डाववर्जिताः /
मन्त्राक्षराणि विश्लिष्य अनुस्वारं नयेत् पृथक् //
324.m: The mātṛkā letters are to be drawn on the ground, free of conjuncts and neuter [vowels]; / having separated the syllables of the mantra, one should set the nasal mark aside.

324.s:
sādhakasya tu yā saṃjñā tasyā viśleṣaṇaṃ caret /
mantrasyādau tathā cānte sādhakārṇāni yojayet //
324.d:
साधकस्य तु या संज्ञा तस्या विश्लेषणं चरेत् /
मन्त्रस्यादौ तथा चान्ते साधकार्णानि योजयेत् //
324.m: One should make an analysis of the name of the practitioner; / one should join the syllables of the practitioner's [name] at the beginning and the end of the mantra.

324.s:
siddhaḥ sādhyaḥ suśiddho 'riḥ saṃjñāto gaṇayet kramāt /
mantrasyādau tathā cānte siddhidaḥ syācchatāṃśataḥ //
324.d:
सिद्धः साध्यः सुशिद्धो ऽरिः संज्ञातो गणयेत् क्रमात् /
मन्त्रस्यादौ तथा चान्ते सिद्धिदः स्याच्छतांशतः //
324.m: One should count in order from the name: siddha, sādhya, susiddha, and ari; / at the beginning and at the end of the mantra, it bestows success by a hundredth portion.

324.s:
siddhādiścāntasiddhaś ca tatkṣaṇādeva sidhyati /
susiddhādiḥ susiddhantaḥsiddhavat parikalpayet //
324.d:
सिद्धादिश्चान्तसिद्धश् च तत्क्षणादेव सिध्यति /
सुसिद्धादिः सुसिद्धन्तःसिद्धवत् परिकल्पयेत् //
324.m: A mantra that is siddha at the beginning and siddha at the end succeeds in that very moment; / one with susiddha at the beginning and susiddha at the end should be considered like siddha.

324.s:
arimādau tathānte ca dūrataḥ parivarjayet /
siddhaḥ susiddhaś caikārthe ariḥ sādhyastathaiva ca //
324.d:
अरिमादौ तथान्ते च दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् /
सिद्धः सुसिद्धश् चैकार्थे अरिः साध्यस्तथैव च //
324.m: One must avoid an enemy from afar, both at the beginning and at the end; / siddha and susiddha have the same result, and similarly ari and sādhya.

324.s:
ādau siddhaḥ sthito mantre tadante tadvadeva hi /
madhye ripusahasrāṇi na doṣāya bhavanti hi //
324.d:
आदौ सिद्धः स्थितो मन्त्रे तदन्ते तद्वदेव हि /
मध्ये रिपुसहस्राणि न दोषाय भवन्ति हि //
324.m: If a siddha is stationed at the beginning of the mantra and likewise at its end, / thousands of enemies in the middle indeed cause no harm.

324.s:
māyāprasādapraṇavenāṃśakaḥ khyātamantrake /
brahmāṃśako brahmavidyā viṣṇvaṅgo(1) vaiṣṇavaḥsmṛtaḥ //
:n
1 viṣṇvaṃśa iti ña..
:p 178
324.d:
मायाप्रसादप्रणवेनांशकः ख्यातमन्त्रके /
ब्रह्मांशको ब्रह्मविद्या विष्ण्वङ्गो(1) वैष्णवःस्मृतः //
:न्
1 विष्ण्वंश इति ञ..
:प् 178
324.m:
In a well-known mantra, the division is determined by māyā, prasāda, and praṇava; / Brahmā's division is the lore of Brahmā; Viṣṇu's portion is remembered as Vaiṣṇava.
[Footnote]
1. "viṣṇvaṃśa" in manuscript ña.. / :p 178

324.s:
rudrāṃśako bhavedvīra indrāṃśaśceśvarapriyaḥ /
nāgāṃśo nāgastabdhākṣo yakṣāṃśo bhūṣaṇapriyaḥ //
324.d:
रुद्रांशको भवेद्वीर इन्द्रांशश्चेश्वरप्रियः /
नागांशो नागस्तब्धाक्षो यक्षांशो भूषणप्रियः //
324.m: Rudra's portion makes one a hero; Indra's portion makes one dear to the lord; / the Nāga-portion has rigid eyes like a serpent; the Yakṣa-portion is fond of ornaments;

324.s:
gandharvāṃśo 'tigītādi bhīmāṃśo rākṣasāṃśakaḥ /
dairyāṃśaḥ syād yuddhakāryo mānī vidyādharāṃśakaḥ //
324.d:
गन्धर्वांशो ऽतिगीतादि भीमांशो राक्षसांशकः /
दैर्यांशः स्याद् युद्धकार्यो मानी विद्याधरांशकः //
324.m: the Gandharva-portion is exceedingly fond of singing; the fierce portion belongs to the Rākṣasas; / the Daitya-portion is inclined to battle; the Vidyādhara-portion is proud;

324.s:
piśācāṃśo malākrānto mantraṃ dadyānnirīkṣya ca /
mantra ekāt phaḍantaḥ syāt vidyāpañcāśatāvadhi //
324.d:
पिशाचांशो मलाक्रान्तो मन्त्रं दद्यान्निरीक्ष्य च /
मन्त्र एकात् फडन्तः स्यात् विद्यापञ्चाशतावधि //
324.m: the Piśāca-portion is overcome by impurity; having examined [this], one should impart the mantra. / A mantra ending in phaṭ may consist of one [syllable]; a vidyā extends up to fifty [syllables].

324.s:
bālā viṃśākṣarāntā ca rudrā dvāviṃśagāyudhā /
tata ūrdhvantu ye mantrā dṛddhā yāvacchatatrayaṃ //
324.d:
बाला विंशाक्षरान्ता च रुद्रा द्वाविंशगायुधा /
तत ऊर्ध्वन्तु ये मन्त्रा दृद्धा यावच्छतत्रयं //
324.m: A bālā-mantra ends at twenty syllables; a rudra-mantra, having weapons, at twenty-two; / the mantras that are beyond that, up to three hundred, are mature.

324.s:
akārādihakārantāḥ kramāt pakṣau sitāsitau /
anusvāravisargeṇa vinā caiva svarā daśa //
324.d:
अकारादिहकारन्ताः क्रमात् पक्षौ सितासितौ /
अनुस्वारविसर्गेण विना चैव स्वरा दश //
324.m: From the letter "a" to the letter "ha" are in succession the two fortnights, light and dark; / and without the nasal mark and visarga, there are ten vowels.

324.s:
hrasvāḥ śuklā dīrghāḥ śyāmāṃstithayaḥpratipammukhāḥ /
udite śāntikādīni bhramite vaśyakādikam //
324.d:
ह्रस्वाः शुक्ला दीर्घाः श्यामांस्तिथयःप्रतिपम्मुखाः /
उदिते शान्तिकादीनि भ्रमिते वश्यकादिकम् //
324.m: Short [vowels] are white, long ones are dark; the lunar days begin with pratipad; / when [the breath is] ascending, rites of pacification and the like [should be done]; when circulating, rites of subjugation and the like;

324.s:
bhrāmite sandhayo dveṣoccāṭane stambhane 'stakam /
ihāvāhe śāntikādyaṃ piṅgale karṣaṇādikam(1) //
324.d:
भ्रामिते सन्धयो द्वेषोच्चाटने स्तम्भने ऽस्तकम् /
इहावाहे शान्तिकाद्यं पिङ्गले कर्षणादिकम्(1) //
324.m: when rotated, junctions, enmity, eradication, and immobilization are the eightfold rites; / during the left flow, rites of pacification and the like; during the right flow, rites of attraction and the like;

324.s:
māraṇoccāṭanādīni viṣuve pañcadhā pṛthak /
adharasya gṛhe pṛthvī ūrdhve tejo 'ntarā dravaḥ //
324.d:
मारणोच्चाटनादीनि विषुवे पञ्चधा पृथक् /
अधरस्य गृहे पृथ्वी ऊर्ध्वे तेजो ऽन्तरा द्रवः //
324.m: liquidation, eradication, and so forth [are done] separately in five ways at the equinox; / in the lower chamber is earth, above is fire, and in between is liquid;

324.s:
randhrapārśve vahirvāyuḥ sarvaṃ vyāpya maheśvaraḥ /
stambhanaṃ pārthive śāntirjale vaśyādi tejase /
vāyau syād bhramaṇaṃ śūnye puṇyaṃ kālaṃ samabhyaset //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe aṃśakādirnāma
caturviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 karṣakādikamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 179
:ś atha pañcaviṃśatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gauryādipūjā
324.d:
रन्ध्रपार्श्वे वहिर्वायुः सर्वं व्याप्य महेश्वरः /
स्तम्भनं पार्थिवे शान्तिर्जले वश्यादि तेजसे /
वायौ स्याद् भ्रमणं शून्ये पुण्यं कालं समभ्यसेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अंशकादिर्नाम
चतुर्विंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 कर्षकादिकमिति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 179
:श् अथ पञ्चविंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
गौर्यादिपूजा
324.m:
at the side of the aperture, wind is outside; Maheśvara pervades everything; / immobilization is in the earthly, pacification in water, subjugation and the like in fire; / roaming occurs in wind; in the void, one should practice at an auspicious time.
Thus ends the three hundred and twenty-fourth chapter, entitled “The Divisions and Related Topics,” in the great Āgneya Purāṇa.

Worship of Gaurī and others.
